children.text: śāntipāṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Peace Invocation (<s>Śāntipāṭha</s>)

children.text:
oṃ vāṅ me manasi pratiṣṭhitā mano me vāci pratiṣṭhitamāvirāvīrmā edhi /
vedasya me āṇīsthaḥ śrutaṃ me mā prahāsīḥ /
anenādhītenāhorātrānsandadhāmyṛtaṃ vadiṣyāmi /
satyaṃ vadiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: I shall speak what is true.

children.text: tanmāmavatu /
children.translated_text: May that protect me.

children.text: tadvaktāramavatu /
children.translated_text: May that protect the teacher.

children.text: avatu māmavatu vaktāramavatu vaktāram //
children.translated_text: May it protect me; may it protect the teacher; may it protect the teacher.

<s>Oṃ</s>. May my speech be established in my mind; may my mind be established in my speech. O Self-luminous One, reveal yourself to me. May you both be the bearers of the <s>Veda</s> to me. May what I have heard not forsake me. By this study I join together day and night. I shall speak what is right.

children.text: oṃ śāntiḥ! śānti!! śāntiḥ!!!
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Peace! Peace!! Peace!!!

children.text: sambandhabhāṣya-
children.translated_text: Introductory Commentary (<s>Sambandhabhāṣya</s>) —

children.text:
parisamāptaṃ karma sahāparabrahmaviṣayavijñānena /
saiṣā karmaṇo jñānasahitasya parā gatirukthavijñānadvāreṇopasaṃhṛtā /
"etatsatyaṃ brahma prāṇākhyam""eṣa eko devaḥ""etasyaiva prāṇasya sarve devā vibhūtayaḥ""etasya prāṇasyātmabhāvaṃ gacchandevatā apyeti"ityuktam /
so 'yaṃ devatāpyayalakṣaṇaḥ paraḥ puruṣārthaḥ, eṣa mokṣaḥ /
sa cāyaṃ yathoktena jñānakarmasamuccayasādhanena prāptavyo nātaḥ paramastītyeke pratipannāḥ /
tānnirācikīrṣuruttaraṃ kevalātmajñānavidhānārtham 'ātmā vā idam' ityādyāha /
children.translated_text: Ritual action (<s>karma</s>), together with the knowledge concerning the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, has been completed [in the preceding portion]. This ultimate goal of action combined with knowledge has been concluded through the knowledge of the <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise): 'This is the true <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Prāṇa</s>' — 'He is the one God' — 'All the gods are the glorious manifestations of this <s>Prāṇa</s> alone' — 'The deity who attains oneness with this <s>Prāṇa</s> enters [into him].' This supreme human goal, characterized by the merging of the deities [into <s>Prāṇa</s>], is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Some have held that this is to be attained through the means of the combination of knowledge and action (<s>jñāna-karma-samuccaya</s>) as described, and that there is nothing higher than this. Desiring to refute them, [the <s>śruti</s>] states '<s>Ātman</s> alone was this [in the beginning]' and so forth, for the purpose of enjoining pure self-knowledge (<s>kevalātmajñāna</s>) in the subsequent [section].

children.text: kathaṃ punarakarmasambandhikevalātmavijñānavidhānārtha uttaro grantha iti gamyate?
children.translated_text: But how is it understood that the subsequent text is for the purpose of enjoining pure self-knowledge unconnected with ritual action?

children.text:
anyārthānavagamāt /
tathā ca pūrvoktānāṃ devatānāmagnyādīnāṃ saṃsāritvaṃ darśayiṣyatyaśanāyādidoṣavattvena"tamaśanāpipāsābhyāmanvavārjam"(1 / 2 / 1) ityādinā /
aśanāyādimatsarvaṃ saṃsāra eva parasya tu brahmaṇo 'śanāyādyatyayaśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because no other purpose can be ascertained. And accordingly, [the text] will show the <s>saṃsāric</s> nature of the previously mentioned deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others, by their being afflicted with hunger and the like, through passages such as 'They encompassed him with hunger and thirst' (1.2.1). Everything that is possessed of hunger and the like is indeed in <s>saṃsāra</s>. But with regard to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, because the <s>śruti</s> declares the transcendence of hunger and the like.

children.text:
bhavatyevaṃ kevalātmajñānaṃ mokṣasādhanaṃ na tvatrākarmyevādhikriyate viśeṣāśravaṇāt /
akarmiṇa āśramyantarasyehāśravaṇāt /
karma ca bṛhatīsahasralakṣaṇaṃ prastutyānantaramevātmajñānaṃ prārabhyate /
tasmāt karmyevādhikriyate /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Granted that pure self-knowledge is the means to liberation, but the person qualified here is not necessarily one who has renounced action, since no such specification is heard. Because no mention is made here of the non-performer of action belonging to another <s>āśrama</s>. Moreover, self-knowledge is commenced immediately after the introduction of <s>karma</s> characterized by the thousand <s>bṛhatī</s> [metres]. Therefore, it is the performer of action alone who is qualified [for this knowledge].

children.text:
na ca karmāsaṃbandhyātmavijñānaṃ pūrvavadanta upasaṃhārāt /
yathā karmasaṃbandhinaḥ puruṣasya sūryātmanaḥ sthāvarajaṅgamādisarvaprāṇyātmatvamuktaṃ brāhmaṇena mantreṇa ca"sūrya ātmā"(ṛ.saṃ.1 / 114 / 1) ityādinā, tathaiva 'eṣa brahmaiṣa indraḥ' (3 / 1 / 3) ityādyupakramya sarvaprāṇyātmatvam 'yacca sthāvaraṃ sarvaṃ tatprajñānetram, (3 / 1 / 3) ityupasaṃhariṣyati /
tathā ca saṃhitopaniṣadi"etaṃ hyeva bahuvṛcā mahatyukthe mīmāṃsante"(ai.ā.3 / 2 / 3 / 12) ityādinā karmasaṃbandhitvamuktvā"sarveṣu bhūteṣvetameva brahmetyācakṣate"ityupasaṃharati /
tathā tasyaiva"yo 'yamaśarīraḥ prajñātmā"ityuktasya"yaścāsāvāditya ekameva taditi vidyāt"ityekatvamuktam /
ihāpi"ko 'yamātmā"(3 / 1 / 1) ityupakramya prajñātmatvameva"prajñānaṃ brahma"(3 / 1 / 3) iti darśayiṣyati /
tasmānnākarmasaṃbandhyātmajñānam /
children.translated_text: [Objection continued:] And the self-knowledge here is not disconnected from action, because at the conclusion [it is related to action] just as before. Just as the Self-hood of all beings including the moving and unmoving was stated for the person connected with action, by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage and the <s>mantra</s> 'The sun is the Self' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 1.114.1) and so forth — in exactly the same way, beginning with 'He is <s>Brahmā</s>, he is <s>Indra</s>' (3.1.3), the text will conclude the Self-hood of all beings with 'and whatever is stationary — all that is guided by consciousness' (3.1.3). And in the <s>Saṃhitopaniṣad</s>, having stated the connection with <s>karma</s> by 'The followers of the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> investigate this in the great <s>uktha</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.3.12) and so forth, it concludes: 'In all beings they declare this alone to be <s>Brahman</s>.' Likewise, for that very [Self] described as 'this one who is bodiless, the cognitive Self,' unity is stated: 'and that which is the sun — one should know that it is one and the same.' Here too, beginning with 'Who is this Self?' (3.1.1), the text will show that [the Self] is of the nature of pure consciousness: 'Consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>' (3.1.3). Therefore, self-knowledge is not disconnected from action.

children.text:
punaruktyānarthakyamiti cet /
katham?"prāṇo vā ahamasmyṛṣe"ityādibrāhmaṇena"sūrya ātmā"iti mantreṇa ca nirdhāritasyātmanaḥ (3 / 1 / 1) iti praśnapūrvakaṃ punarnirdhāraṇaṃ punaruktamanarthakamiti cet na; tasyaiva dharmāntaraviśeṣanirdhāraṇārthatvānna punaruktatādoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, there is the fault of purposeless repetition. How? The Self already ascertained by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage 'I am indeed <s>Prāṇa</s>, O sage' and by the <s>mantra</s> 'The sun is the Self' — the re-ascertainment of that [Self] through the question 'Who is this Self?' (3.1.1) would be purposeless repetition. [Reply:] No; because the purpose is to ascertain particular additional properties of that very [Self], there is no fault of repetition.

children.text:
katham? tasyaiva karmasaṃbandhino jagatsṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārādidharmaviśeṣanirdhāraṇārthatvāt kevalopāstyarthatvādvā /
athavā ātmetyādiparo granthasandarbha ātmanaḥ karmiṇaḥ karmaṇo 'nyatropāsanāprāptau karmaprastāve 'vihitatvātkevalo 'pyātmopāsya ityevamarthaḥ /
bhedābhedopāsyatvādvaika evātmā karmaviṣaye bhedadṛṣṭibhāk, sa evākarmakāle 'bhedenāpyupāsya ityevamapunaruktatā /
children.translated_text: How? Because the purpose is to ascertain the particular properties — such as the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe — of that same [Self] connected with action; or because it serves the purpose of mere worship (<s>upāsti</s>). Or alternatively, the compilation of texts beginning with 'the Self' has this meaning: when the performer of action (<s>karmin</s>) cannot attain worship of the Self apart from action in the context of the ritual, the Self alone is [nevertheless] to be worshipped, since it is enjoined [independently]. Since the same one Self is worshippable through [both] difference and non-difference — the one Self partakes of the vision of difference in the context of ritual, and that same [Self] is also to be worshipped through non-difference at the time of non-action — thus there is no repetition.

children.text:
"vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca yastadvedobhayaṃ saha /
avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayāmṛtamaśnute"(ī.u.11) iti,"kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ"(ī.u.2) iti ca vājinām /
na ca varṣaśatātparamāyurmartyānām /
yena karmaparityāgenātmānamupāsīta /
darśitaṃ ca"tāvanti puruṣāyuṣo 'hnāṃ sahasrāṇi bhavanti"iti /
varṣaśataṃ cāyuḥ karmaṇaiva vyāptam /
darśitaśca mantraḥ"kurvanneveha karmāṇi"ityādiḥ /
tathā"yāvajjīvamagnihotrañjuhoti""yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta"ityādyāśca /
"taṃ yajñapātrairdahanti"iti ca /
ṛṇatrayaśruteśca /
tatra pārivrājyādi śāstraṃ vyutthāyātha bhikṣācaryaṃ caranti (bṛ.u.3 / 5 / 1, 4 / 4 / 22) iti ātmajñānastutiparor'thavādaḥ /
anadhikṛtārtho vā /
children.translated_text: 'One who knows both knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) together — crossing over death by ignorance, one attains immortality by knowledge' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 11), and 'Performing actions here indeed, one should wish to live a hundred years' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 2) — thus [say] the <s>Vājins</s>. The lifespan of mortals does not exceed a hundred years — [so there is no time] during which, by abandoning action, one would worship the Self. And it has been shown: 'So many are the thousands of days in a person's lifetime.' And the lifespan of a hundred years is entirely occupied by <s>karma</s>. The <s>mantra</s> has been cited: 'Performing actions here indeed' and so forth. And likewise: 'One should offer the <s>agnihotra</s> as long as one lives,' 'One should sacrifice with the <s>darśa</s> and <s>pūrṇamāsa</s> as long as one lives,' and so on. And: 'They burn him with the sacrificial vessels.' And because of the <s>śruti</s> about the three debts. Regarding the scriptural passages about renunciation (<s>pārivrajya</s>), such as 'Having risen above, they then lead the life of mendicancy' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.5.1; 4.4.22) — these are <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic passages) devoted to praising self-knowledge. Or they pertain to those not [otherwise] qualified.

children.text:
na; paramārthavijñāne phalādarśane kriyānupapatteḥ /
yaduktaṃ karmiṇa ātmajñānaṃ karmasaṃbandhi ca ityādi tanna /
paraṃ hyāptakāmaṃ sarvasaṃsāradoṣavarjitaṃ brahmāhamasmītyātmatvena vijñāne, kṛtena kartavyena vā prayojanamātmano 'paśyata phalādarśane kriyā nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: [Reply:] No; because when one has the knowledge of the ultimate reality, since no fruit [of action] is seen, action is untenable. The assertion that the self-knowledge of the performer of action is connected with action and so forth — that is not [correct]. For when one knows through identity with the Self: 'I am <s>Brahman</s> — the supreme, the one whose desires are fulfilled, free from all the defects of <s>saṃsāra</s>' — since one sees no purpose for oneself through what has been done or what is to be done, and since no fruit [of action] is seen, action is untenable.

children.text:
phalādarśane 'pi niyuktatvātkarotīti cenna niyogāviṣayātmadarśanāt /
iṣṭayogamaniṣṭaviyogaṃ cātmanaḥ prayojanaṃ paśyaṃstadupāyārthī yo bhavati sa niyogasya viṣayo dṛṣṭo loke /
na tu tadviparītaniyogāviṣayabrahmātmatvadarśī /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even though no fruit is seen, one acts because one is enjoined. [Reply:] No; because one who sees the Self [as <s>Brahman</s>] is outside the scope of injunction. In the world, one who sees the conjunction with the desired and the disjunction from the undesired as the purpose for the self, and who seeks the means thereto — such a one is observed to be the object of injunction. But not the one who sees the Self as <s>Brahman</s>, who is the opposite of that and outside the scope of injunction.

children.text:
brahmātmatvadarśyapi saṃścenniyujyeta niyogāviṣayo 'pi sanna kaścinna niyukta iti sarvaṃ karma sarveṇa sarvadā kartavyaṃ prapnoti /
taccāniṣṭam /
na ca sa niyoktuṃ śakyate kenacit; āmnāyasyāpi tatprabhavatvāt /
ma hi svavijñānotthena vacasā svayaṃ niyujyate /
nāpi bṛhavitsvāmyavivekinā bhṛtyena /
children.translated_text: If even one who sees the Self as <s>Brahman</s> could somehow be enjoined, then since even those outside the scope of injunction would not be exempt, it would follow that all actions must be performed by everyone at all times. And that is undesirable. Nor can he be enjoined by anything, since even the <s>Veda</s> originates from that [<s>Brahman</s>]. For one is not enjoined by oneself through the speech that arises from one's own knowledge. Nor by a servant who does not distinguish [itself from] its own master.

children.text:
āmnāyasya nityatve sati svātaṃntryātsarvānprati niyoktṛtvasāmarthyamiti cenna uktadoṣāt /
tathāpi sarveṇa sarvadā sarvamaviśiṣṭaṃ karma kartavyamityukto doṣo 'pyaparihārya eva /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Since the <s>Veda</s> is eternal, by its independence it has the capacity to enjoin all. [Reply:] No; because of the stated fault. Even so, the stated fault — that all action without distinction must be performed by everyone at all times — would be unavoidable.

children.text:
tadapi śāstreṇaiva vidhīyata iti ced yathākarmakartavyatā śāstreṇa kṛtā tathā tadapyātmajñānaṃ tasyaiva karmiṇaḥ śāstreṇa vidhīyata iti cet, na; viruddhārthabodhakatvānupapatteḥ /
na hyekasminkṛtākṛtasaṃbandhitvaṃ tadviparītatvaṃ ca bodhayituṃ śakyam, śītoṣṇatāmivāgneḥ /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If it is said that this [discrimination] too is enjoined by scripture alone — just as the obligation to perform action is established by scripture, so too is self-knowledge enjoined by scripture for that very performer of action — [Reply:] No; because it is impossible for [the same scripture] to teach contradictory meanings. For it is not possible to teach regarding the same [entity] both relatedness to what is done and what is to be done, and its opposite — like [teaching] both coldness and heat of fire.

children.text:
na ceṣṭayogacikīrṣā ātmano 'niṣṭaviyogācikīrṣā ca śāstrakṛtā, sarvaprāṇināṃ taddarśanāt /
śāstrakṛtaṃ cettadubhayaṃ gopālādīnāṃ na dṛśyeta, aśāstrajñatvātteṣām /
yaddhi svato 'prāptaṃ tacchāstreṇa bodhayitavyam /
taccetkṛtakartavyatāvirodhyātmajñānaṃ śāstreṇa kṛtam, kathaṃ tadviruddhāṃ kartavyatāṃ punarutpādayecchītatāmivāgnau tama iva ca bhānau /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the desire for conjunction with what is desired and the desire for disjunction from what is undesired are not created by scripture, since all living beings are seen to have them. If they were created by scripture, those two would not be seen in cowherds and the like, since they are ignorant of scripture. For that which is not available by itself is what scripture must teach. And if self-knowledge, which contradicts the obligation to act, is produced by scripture, how could [scripture] again produce the obligation to act that contradicts it — like coldness in fire and darkness in the sun?

children.text:
na bodhayatyeveti cenna,"sa ma ātmeti vidyāt"(kau.u.3 / 9) "prajñānaṃ brahma"(3 / 1 / 3) iti copasaṃhārāt /
"tadātmānamevāvet"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 9) "tattvamasi"(chā.u.6 / 8 -16) ityevamādivākyānāṃ tatparatvāt /
utpannasya ca brahmātmavijñānasyābādhyamānatvānnānutpannaṃ bhrāntaṃ veti śakyaṃ vaktum /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Scripture simply does not teach [self-knowledge]. [Reply:] No; because of the conclusion: 'One should know him as my Self' (<s>Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad</s> 3.9) and 'Consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>' (3.1.3). Because sentences such as 'He knew the Self alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.9), 'You are that' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8-16), and the like are devoted to that [self-knowledge]. And since the knowledge of the Self as <s>Brahman</s>, once arisen, is not sublated, it cannot be said to be either non-arisen or erroneous.

children.text:
tyāge 'pi prayojanābhāvasya tulyatvamiti cet"nākṛteneha kaścana"(gītā 3 / 28) iti smṛteḥ ya āhurviditvā brahma vyutthānameva kuryāditi teṣāmapyeṣa samāno doṣaḥ prayojanābhāva iti cenna; akriyāmātratvād vyutthānasya /
avidyānimitto hi prayojanasya bhāvo na vastudharmaḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ taddarśanāt /
prayojanatṛṣṇayā ca preryamāṇasya vāṅmanaḥkāyaiḥ pravṛttidarśanāt /
"so 'kāmayata jāyā me syāt"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 17) ityādinā putravittādi pāṅktalakṣaṇaṃ kāmyameveti"ubhe hyete eṣaṇe eva"(bṛ.u.3 / 5 / 1 ; 4 / 4 / 22) iti vājasaneyibrāhmaṇe 'vadhāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even in the case of renunciation, there is the same [fault of] absence of purpose. [Answer to those who claim,] citing the <s>smṛti</s> 'No one here [exists] without action' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 3.28), that those who say 'having known <s>Brahman</s>, one should simply rise above [action]' — for them too this is the same fault, namely absence of purpose. [Reply:] No; because rising above [action] is merely the absence of action. For the existence of purpose is caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), not a property of reality, since this is seen in all living beings. And because one who is impelled by the craving for purpose is seen to engage through speech, mind, and body. Because the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>) determines, by 'He desired: may I have a wife' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.17) and so forth, that what is desired — sons, wealth, and the like, which characterize the five-layered [worldly existence] — are indeed [mere] desires: 'For both of these are indeed desires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.5.1; 4.4.22).

children.text:
avidyākāmadoṣanimittāyā vāṅmanaḥkāyapravṛtteḥ pāṅktalakṣaṇāyā viduṣo 'vidyādidoṣābhāvādanupapatteḥ kriyābhāvamātraṃ vyutthānam, na tu yāgādivadanuṣṭheyarūpaṃ bhāvātmakam /
tacca vidyāvatpuruṣadharma iti na prayojanamanveṣṭavyam /
na hi tamasi pravṛttasyodita āloke yadgartapaṅkakaṇṭakādyatapanaṃ tatkiṃprayojanamiti praśnārham /
children.translated_text:
Since the activity of speech, mind, and body — which has the five-fold character and is caused by the defects of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, etc. — is untenable for the knower due to the absence of defects such as <s>avidyā</s>, cessation (<s>vyutthāna</s>) is merely the absence of action, not something of a positive nature to be performed like sacrifice and the like.
And that [cessation] is a property of the person who possesses knowledge, so no purpose need be sought [for it].
For when one who has been walking in darkness [comes into] risen light, the avoidance of pits, mud, thorns, etc. is not a matter worthy of the question 'what is its purpose?'

children.text:
vyutthānaṃ tarhyarthaprāptatvānna codanārhamiti gārhasthye cetparaṃ brahmavijñānaṃ jātaṃ tatraivāstvakurvata āsanaṃ na tato 'nyatra gamanamiti cenna kāmaprayuktatvādgārhasthyasya"etāvānvai kāmaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 17) iti"ubhe hyete eṣaṇe eva"(bṛ,u.3 / 5 / 1 ; 4 / 4 / 22) ityavadhāraṇāt /
kāmanimittaputravittādisaṃbandhaniyamābhāvamātraṃ na hi tato 'nyatra gamanaṃ vyutthānamucyate /
ato na gārhasthya evākurvata āsanamutpannavidyasya /
etena guruśuśrūṣātapasorapyapratipattirviduṣaḥsiddhā /
children.translated_text:
If cessation, being a matter naturally arrived at, is not worthy of injunction — then if the supreme knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> arises while in the householder stage, let one remain there itself, sitting without acting, and not go elsewhere — this is not so, because the householder state is motivated by desire, as [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'This much alone indeed is desire' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.17), and because of the definitive statement 'For these two are indeed desires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.5.1; 4.4.22).
Cessation is merely the absence of the fixed connection with sons, wealth, etc. motivated by desire — it is not said that going elsewhere [constitutes] cessation.
Therefore, one who has attained knowledge does not sit [inactive] in the householder stage alone.
By this, the non-performance of service to the teacher and austerities is also established for the knower.

children.text: atra kecid gṛhasthā bhikṣāṭanādibhayātparibhavācca trasyamānāḥ sūkṣmadṛṣṭitāṃ darśayanta uttaramāhuḥ bhikṣorapi bhikṣāṭanadiniyamadarśanāddehadhāraṇamātrārthino gṛhasthasyāpi sādhyasādhanaiṣaṇobhayavinirmuktasya dehamātradhāraṇarthamaśanācchādanamātramupajīvato gṛha evāstvāsanamiti /
children.translated_text: Here, some householders, trembling from fear of begging and from [social] humiliation, display subtle discernment and state a further [argument]: since even for the mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) no fixed rule of begging etc. is seen — the householder too, whose only aim is the maintenance of the body, who is free from the two pursuits of ends and means, subsisting on mere food and clothing for the purpose of merely maintaining the body, may remain sitting at home itself.

children.text:
na, svagṛhaviśeṣaparigrahaniyamasya kāmaprayuktatvādityuktottarametat /
svagṛhaviśeṣaparigrahābhāve ca śarīradhāraṇamātraprayuktāśanācchādanārthinaḥ svaparigrahaviśeṣābhāver'thādbhikṣukatvameva /
children.translated_text:
No — this has already been answered: because the adherence to a particular household is motivated by desire.
And in the absence of adherence to a particular household, one who seeks food and clothing solely for the purpose of maintaining the body, being free from particular possessions, is indeed a mendicant (<s>bhikṣuka</s>) by that very fact.

children.text:
śarīradhāraṇārthāyāṃ bhikṣāṭanādipravṛttau yathā niyamo bhikṣoḥ śaucādau ca, tathā gṛhiṇo 'pi viduṣo 'kāmino 'stu nityakarmasu niyamena pravṛttiryāvajjīvādiśrutiniyuktatvāt pratyavāyaparihārāyeti /
etanniyogāviṣayatvena viduṣaḥ pratyuktamaśakyaniyojyatvācceti /
children.translated_text:
If [it be said]: just as the mendicant has fixed rules regarding begging and purity, etc., so too let the householder who is a knower and is free from desire have obligatory engagement in daily rites (<s>nityakarma</s>), since he is enjoined by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'as long as one lives' and to avoid adverse consequences (<s>pratyavāya</s>) —
this has been answered by [showing] that the knower is outside the domain of injunction, because he cannot be enjoined.

children.text: yāvajjīvādinityacodanānarthakyamiti cet?
children.translated_text: If [it be objected]: the perpetual injunctions such as 'as long as one lives' would be purposeless —

children.text:
na, avidvadviṣayatvenārthavattvāt /
yattu bhikṣoḥ śarīradhāraṇamātrapravṛttasya pravṛtterniyatatvaṃ tatpravṛtterna prayojakam /
ācamanapravṛttasya pipāsāpagamavannānyaprayojanārthatvamavagamyate /
na cāgnihotrādīnāṃ tadvadarthaprāptapravṛttiniyatatvopapattiḥ /
children.translated_text:
No, because they are meaningful as pertaining to the non-knower.
As for the fixed character of the activity of the mendicant who is engaged merely in maintaining the body — that is not caused by [Vedic] injunction.
It is understood like the subsiding of thirst for one engaged in sipping water — not as being for the purpose of another end.
And for the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, the fixed character of activity as naturally arrived at is not tenable [in the same way].

children.text: arthaprāptapravṛttiniyamo 'pi prayojanābhāve 'nupapanna eveti cet?
children.translated_text: If [it be said]: even the fixed character of naturally arrived-at activity is untenable in the absence of a purpose —

children.text:
na, tanniyamasya pūrvapravṛttisiddhatvāttadatikrame yatnagauravāt /
arthaprāptasya vyutthānasya punarvacanādviduṣaḥ kartavyatvopapattiḥ /
aviduṣopi mumukṣuṇā pārivrājyaṃ kartavyameva /
tathā ca"śānto dāntaḥ"(bṛ.u.4 / 4 / 23) ityādivacanaṃ pramāṇam /
śamadamādīnāṃ cātmadarśanasādhanānāmanyāśrameṣvanupapatteḥ /
"atyāśramibhyaḥ parama pavitraṃ provāca samyagṛṣisaṃghajuṣṭam"(6 / 21) iti ca śvetāśvatare vijñāyate /
'na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvamānaśuḥ' (kaivalya.2) iti ca kaivalyaśrutiḥ /
"jñātvā naiṣkarmyamācaret"iti ca smṛteḥ /
"brahmāśramapade vaset"iti ca brahmacaryādividyāsādhanānāṃ ca sākalyenātyāśramiṣūpapattergrārhasthye 'saṃbhavāt /
na cāsaṃpannaṃ sādhanaṃ kasyacidarthasya sādhanāyālam /
yadvijñānopayogīni ca gārhasthyāśramakarmāṇi teṣāṃ paramaphalamupasaṃhṛtaṃ devatāpyayalakṣaṇaṃ saṃsāraviṣayameva /
yadi karmiṇa eva paramātmavijñānamabhaviṣyat saṃsāraviṣayasyaiva phalasyopasaṃhāro nopāpātsyat /
children.translated_text:
No, because the fixedness of that [activity] is established by prior practice, and because transgressing it requires great effort.
From the re-statement of cessation, which is naturally arrived at, the obligatoriness for the knower is established.
Even the non-knower who desires liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) must adopt the life of wandering renunciation (<s>pārivrājya</s>).
And thus the statement 'tranquil, self-restrained' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.23) etc. is the authority.
Because tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-restraint (<s>dama</s>), and the like, which are the means for the vision of the Self, are untenable in other stages of life.
And in the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s> [Upaniṣad] it is known: 'To those beyond the stages of life (<s>atyāśramin</s>), supremely purifying, well-practiced by assemblies of sages, He taught' (6.21).
And the <s>Kaivalya</s> <s>śruti</s>: 'Not by action, not by progeny, not by wealth — by renunciation alone some attained immortality' (<s>Kaivalya</s> 2).
And from the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Having known, one should practice actionlessness (<s>naiṣkarmya</s>).'
And 'One should dwell in the stage of <s>Brahman</s> [i.e., <s>sannyāsa</s>]' — because the means of knowledge, such as celibacy and the like, are fully tenable only among those beyond the stages of life, and not possible in the householder stage.
And an incomplete means is not capable of accomplishing any purpose.
And as for those householder-stage actions that are useful for knowledge — their ultimate fruit has been concluded as being of the nature of merger with the deities, which pertains to <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) alone.
If knowledge of the Supreme Self were to arise only for the ritualist, the conclusion of a fruit pertaining to <s>saṃsāra</s> alone would not have been appropriate.

children.text:
aṅgaphalaṃ taditi cenna tadvirodhyātmavastuviṣayatvādātmavidyāyāḥ /
nirākṛtasarvanāmarūpakarmaparamārthātmavastuviṣayaṃ jñānamamṛtatvasādhanam /
guṇaphalasaṃbandhe hi nirākṛtasarvaviśeṣātmavastuviṣayatvaṃ jñānasya na prāpnoti /
taccāniṣṭam,"yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūt"
children.translated_text:
If [it be said]: that [saṃsāric fruit] is [merely] an ancillary result — no, because the knowledge of the Self (<s>ātmavidyā</s>) has as its object the reality of the Self, which is opposed to that [saṃsāric result].
Knowledge that is the means to immortality has as its object the ultimate reality of the Self in which all names, forms, and actions are negated.
For if [knowledge] were connected with a subsidiary result, its having as object the reality of the Self in which all distinctions are negated would not be attainable.
And that [consequence] is undesirable — 'When for him everything has become the Self alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14) —

children.text:
(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14) ityadhikṛtya kriyākārakaphalādisarvavyavahāranirākāraṇādviduṣaḥ /
tadviparītasyāviduṣo"yatra hi dvaitamiva"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14) ityuktvā kriyākārakaphalarūpasyaiva saṃsārasya darśitatvācca vājasaneyibrāhmaṇe /
tathehāpi devatāpyayaṃ saṃsāraviṣayaṃ yatphalamaśanāyādimadvastvātmakaṃ tatphalamupasaṃhṛtya kevalaṃ sarvātmakavastuviṣayaṃ jñānamamṛtatvāya vakṣyāmīti pravartate /
children.translated_text:
having taken up [that passage], the negation of all transactional activity involving action, agent, result, etc. is [shown] for the knower in the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s>.
And because, having said 'Where there is, as it were, duality' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14) for the non-knower who is the opposite of that [knower], <s>saṃsāra</s> in the form of action, agent, and result has been shown [for the non-knower].
Likewise here too, having concluded the fruit — which pertains to <s>saṃsāra</s>, consisting of the merger with deities, and consisting of objects such as food, etc. — [the text] proceeds [saying]: 'I shall teach the knowledge that has as its object solely the reality that is the Self of all, for the sake of immortality.'

children.text:
ṛṇapratibandhasyāviduṣa eva manuṣyapitṛdevalokaprāptiṃ prati, na viduṣaḥ /
"so 'yaṃ manuṣyalokaḥ putreṇaiva"(bṛ.u.1 / 5 / 16) ityādilokatrayasādhananiyamaśruteḥ /
viduṣaśca ṛṇapratibandhābhāvo darśita ātmalokārthinaḥ"kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmaḥ"(bṛ.u.4 / 4 / 22) ityādinā /
tathā"etadva sma vai tadvidvāṃsa āhurṛṣaḥ kāvaṣeyāḥ"ityādi /
"etaddha sma vai tatpūrve vidvāṃso 'gnihotraṃ na juhavāñcakruḥ"(kauṣī. 2 / 5) iti ca kauṣītakinām /
aviduṣastarhi ṛṇānapākaraṇe pārivrājyānupapattiriti cet?
children.translated_text:
The obstruction by debts pertains only to the non-knower with respect to attaining the worlds of men, ancestors, and gods — not to the knower.
Because of the <s>śruti</s> fixing the means for attaining the three worlds: 'This world of men is [attained] by the son alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.5.16), etc.
And the absence of obstruction by debts for the knower has been shown — for one who seeks the world of the Self: 'What shall we do with progeny?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.22), etc.
Likewise: 'This indeed the knowers, the sages of the <s>Kavaṣa</s> [lineage], used to say,' etc.
And of the <s>Kauṣītakins</s>: 'Indeed, the ancient knowers did not offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 2.5).
If [it be objected]: for the non-knower, renunciation is untenable without repaying the debts —

children.text:
na; prāggārhasthyapratipatterṛṇitvāsaṃbhavāt /
adhikārānārūḍho 'pyṛṇī ca syāt sarvasya ṛṇitvamityaniṣṭaṃ prasajyetāpratipannagārhasthyasyāpi"gṛhādvanībhūtvā pravrajedyadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajed gṛhādvā vanādvā"(jā.u.4) ityātmadarśanopāyasādhanatveneṣyata eva pārivrājyam /
yāvajjīvādiśrutīnāmavidvadamumukṣuviṣaye kṛtārthatā /
chāndogye ca keṣāñcid dvādaśarātramagnihotraṃ hutvā tata ūrdhva parityāgaḥ śrūyate /
children.translated_text:
No, because before entering the householder stage, the state of being a debtor is impossible.
If even one who has not undertaken the [householder] duty were a debtor, the unwanted consequence would follow that everyone is a debtor.
'Having become a forest-dweller from the household, one should go forth [as a renunciant]; or otherwise, one should go forth directly from the student stage, or from the household, or from the forest' (<s>Jābāla Upaniṣad</s> 4) — thus renunciation is desired precisely as a means for the vision of the Self.
The <s>śrutis</s> concerning 'as long as one lives' etc. are fulfilled as pertaining to the non-knower who does not desire liberation.
And in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, for some, after performing the <s>Agnihotra</s> for twelve days, renunciation thereafter is heard.

children.text:
yattvanadhikṛtānāṃ pārivrājyamiti, tanna, teṣāṃ pṛthageva,"utsannāgniranagniko vā"ityādiśravaṇāt /
sarvasmṛtiṣu cāviśeṣeṇāśramavikalpaḥ prasiddhaḥ samuccayaśca /
children.translated_text:
As for [the objection] that renunciation is for those not [yet] qualified — that is not so, because for those [qualified ones], separately, it is heard: 'one whose fires have been extinguished, or one without fire,' etc.
And in all the <s>smṛtis</s>, the option among the stages of life (<s>āśramas</s>) as well as the combination [of their practices] is well known without distinction.

children.text:
yattu viduṣor'thaprāptaṃ vyutthānamityaśāstrārthatve, gṛhe vane vā tiṣṭhato na viśeṣa iti, tadasat vyutthānasyaivārthaprāptatvānnānyatrāvasthānaṃ syāt /
anyatrāvasthānasya kāmakarmaprayuktatvaṃ hyavocāma, tadabhāvamātraṃ vyutthānamiti ca /
children.translated_text:
As for [the claim] that cessation is naturally arrived at for the knower and thus not a matter of scripture, [and therefore] there is no difference whether one stays at home or in the forest — that is wrong; precisely because cessation alone is naturally arrived at, there would be no staying elsewhere.
For we have stated that staying elsewhere is motivated by desire and action, and cessation is merely the absence of that.

children.text:
yathākāmitvaṃ tu viduṣo 'tyantamaprāptaṃ atyantamūḍhaviṣayatvenāvagamāt /
tathā śāstracoditamapi karma ātmavido 'prāptaṃ gurubhāratayāvagamyate /
kimutātyantāvivekanimittaṃ yathākarmitvam /
na hi unmādatimiradṛṣṭyupalabdhaṃ vastu tadapagame 'pi tathaiva syāt /
unmādatimiradṛṣṭinimittatvādeva tasya /
tasmādātmavido vyutthānavyatirekeṃ na yathākāmitvaṃ na cānyatkartavyamityetatsiddham /
children.translated_text:
The state of being free from desire (<s>yathākāmitva</s>) of the knower is completely untenable, because it is understood as pertaining to one who is completely deluded.
Likewise, even scripturally enjoined action is untenable for the knower of the Self, being understood as a heavy burden.
How much more so the state of acting as a ritualist, which is caused by complete lack of discrimination!
For an object perceived through the sight of madness or eye-disease would not remain the same even when that [condition] has passed.
Because that [perception] is caused precisely by the sight of madness or eye-disease.
Therefore, it is established that for the knower of the Self, apart from cessation, there is neither the state of acting according to desire nor anything else to be done.

children.text:
yattu"vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca yasyadvedobhayaṃ saha"(ī.u.11) iti na vidyāvato vidyayā sahāvidyāpi vartate ityayamarthaḥ kastarhi ekasminpuruṣe ete ekadaiva na saha saṃbadhyeyātāmityarthaḥ /
yathā śuktikāyāṃ rajataśuktikājñāne ekasya puruṣasya /
"dūramete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā"(ka.u.1 / 2 / 4) iti hi kāṭhake /
tasmānna vidyāyāṃ satyāmavidyāsaṃbhavo 'sti /
children.translated_text:
As for 'He who knows both knowledge and ignorance together' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 11) — the meaning is not that for one who possesses knowledge, ignorance too persists along with knowledge. Rather, the meaning is: who indeed is that single person in whom these two would be conjoined simultaneously?
Just as the cognitions of silver and mother-of-pearl [occur] for one person with respect to a mother-of-pearl shell [but not simultaneously].
For in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [Upaniṣad]: 'These two, far apart, going in opposite directions — that which is known as ignorance and that which is known as knowledge' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.4).
Therefore, when knowledge exists, the existence of ignorance is impossible.

children.text:
"tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva"(tai.u.3 / 2) ityādiśruteḥ tapa ādi vidyotpattisādhanaṃ gurūpāsanādi ca karma avidyātmakatvādavidyocyate tena vidyāmutpādya mṛtyuṃ kāmamatitarati /
tato niṣkāmastyaktaiṣaṇobrahmavidyayā amṛtatvamaśnuta itye 'tamartha darśayannāha -"avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayāmṛtamaśnute"(ī.u.11) iti /
children.translated_text:
From the <s>śruti</s> 'Seek to know <s>Brahman</s> through austerity' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 3.2), etc., austerity and the like, as well as service to the teacher and other actions, are means for the arising of knowledge; since they are of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), they are called '<s>avidyā</s>.' Having produced knowledge through them, one crosses over death and desire.
Then, being desireless, having abandoned all pursuits, through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, one attains immortality — showing this meaning, [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'Having crossed over death by <s>avidyā</s>, one attains immortality by <s>vidyā</s>' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 11).

children.text:
yattu puruṣāyuḥ sarvaṃ karmaṇaiva vyāptaṃ"kuvenneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ"(ī.u.2) iti tadavidvadviṣayatvena parihṛtamitarathāsaṃbhavāt /
yattu vakṣyamāṇamapi pūrvoktatulyatvātkarmaṇāviruddhamātmajñānamiti, tatsaviśeṣanirviśeṣātmatayā pratyuktam, uttaratra vyākhyāne ca darśayiṣyāmaḥ /
ataḥ kevalaniṣkriyabrahmātmakatvavidyādarśanārthamuttaro grantha ārabhyate -
children.translated_text: As for the objection that the entire span of a person's life is pervaded by action alone, as stated "One should desire to live a hundred years performing actions" (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 2), that has been set aside as pertaining only to the ignorant, since otherwise it would be impossible. As for the further objection that even the teaching to follow also, being similar to the preceding, shows that knowledge of the Self is not incompatible with action — that has been answered by the distinction between the qualified and the unqualified Self, and we shall demonstrate this in the commentary that follows. Therefore, the subsequent text is begun for the purpose of showing the knowledge that the Self is nothing but actionless <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: START 1,1.1
children.translated_text: [START 1,1.1]

children.text:
ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīt |
nānyat kiñcana miṣat |
sa īkṣata lokān nu sṛjā iti || AitUp_1,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: The Self alone indeed was this [universe] in the beginning, one only. There was nothing else whatsoever that blinked. He deliberated: 'Let me now create the worlds.' (AitUp 1.1.1)

children.text: AitUpBh_1,1.1
children.translated_text: [AitUpBh 1,1.1]

children.text:
ātmā āpnoteratteratatervā paraḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktiraśanāyādisarvasaṃsāradharmavarjito nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvo 'jo 'jaro 'maromṛto 'bhayo 'dvayo vai idaṃ yaduktaṃ nāmarūpakarmabhedabhinnañjagadātmaivaiko 'gre jagataḥ sṛṣṭeḥ prāgāsīt /
kiṃ nedānīṃ sa evaikaḥ
na /
kathaṃ tarhyāsīdityucyate yadyapīdānīṃ sa evaikastathāpyasti viśeṣaḥ /
prāgutpatteravyākṛtanāmarūpabhedamātmabhūtamātmaikaśabdapratyayagocaraṃ jagadidānīṃ vyākṛtanāmarūpabhedatvādanekaśabdapratyayagocaramātmaikaśabdapratyayagocara ceti viśeṣaḥ /
yathā salilātpṛthakphenanāmarūpavyākaraṇātprāksalilaikaśabdapratyayagocarameva phenam, yadā salilātpṛthaṅnāmarūpabhedena vyākṛtaṃ bhavati tadā salilaṃ phenaṃ cetyanekaśabdapratyayabhāksalilameveti caikaśabdapratyayabhākca phenaṃ bhavati tadvat /
nānyatkiñcana na kiñcidapi miṣannimiṣadvyāpāravaditaradvā /
yathā sāṃkhyānāmanātmapakṣapāti svatantraṃ pradhānaṃ yathā ca kāṇādānāmaṇavo na tadvadihānyadātmanaḥ kiñcidapi vastu vidyate kiṃ tarhi ! ātmaivaika āsīdityabhiprāyaḥ /
sa sarvajñasvābhāvyād ātmā eka eva sannīkṣata /
nanu prāgutpatterakāryakaraṇatvātkathamīkṣitavān /
nāyaṃ doṣaḥ sarvajñasvābhāvyāt tathā ca mantravarṇaḥ-"apāṇipādo javano grahītā"(śve.u.3 / 19) ityādiḥ /
kenābhiprāyeṇetyāha - lokān ambhaḥprabhṛtīn prāṇikarmaphalopabhogasthānabhūtānnu sṛjai sṛje 'hamiti //1//
children.translated_text: With what intention [did He deliberate]? To this he says: 'Let me create the worlds' — the worlds beginning with <s>ambhas</s>, which serve as the locus for the experience of the fruits of living beings' actions — 'let me create,' meaning 'I shall create.' (1)

The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) — derived from the roots āp (to pervade), at (to go constantly), or ad (to enjoy) — is the supreme, omniscient, omnipotent one, free from all <s>saṃsāra</s>-attributes such as hunger, eternally pure, awakened, and liberated by nature, unborn, undecaying, immortal, deathless, fearless, non-dual — this world, differentiated into distinctions of name, form, and action, was indeed the <s>Ātman</s> alone, one only, before the creation of the universe. Does He not exist as that same one even now? No [it is not that He does not]. Then why is it said 'was'? Although even now He is that same one, there is nevertheless a distinction. Before origination, the world, whose name-and-form distinctions were unevolved, being of the nature of the Self, was apprehended by the single word and concept 'Self' alone; now, because of having evolved name-and-form distinctions, it is apprehended by many words and concepts, and also by the single word and concept 'Self' — this is the distinction. Just as foam, before the evolution of its distinct name and form as separate from water, is apprehended by the single word and concept 'water' alone, but when it becomes evolved with its distinct name and form as separate from water, then it is apprehended by many words and concepts as 'water' and 'foam,' and also by the single word and concept 'water' alone — so it is here. 'There was nothing else whatsoever' — not even anything blinking, i.e., having the activity of blinking, or anything other [than the Self]. Not like the independent <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, which sides with the non-Self, nor like the atoms of the <s>Kāṇādas</s> (Vaiśeṣikas) — here there exists nothing whatsoever other than the Self. What then? The intended meaning is: the Self alone, one only, existed. He — that Self, being one alone, by virtue of His inherent omniscience — deliberated. But before origination, since there were no effects or instruments, how could He have deliberated? This is no defect, because of His inherent omniscience; and so the <s>mantra</s> text states: 'Without hands and feet, He is swift and a grasper' (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 3.19), and so on.

children.text: START 1,1.2
children.translated_text: [START 1,1.2]

children.text: evamīkṣitvā ālocya -
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, having reflected —

children.text:
sa imāṃl lokān asṛjatāmbho marīcīr maram āpaḥ |
ado 'mbhaḥ pareṇa divam |
dyauḥ pratiṣṭhā |
antarikṣaṃ marīcayaḥ |
pṛthivī maraḥ |
yā adhastāt tā āpaḥ || AitUp_1,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: He created these worlds: <s>ambhas</s> (the waters above), <s>marīcīs</s> (light-rays), <s>mara</s> (the mortal realm), and <s>āpas</s> (the waters below). That which is beyond heaven is <s>ambhas</s>. Heaven is the support. The mid-region is the <s>marīcis</s>. The earth is <s>mara</s>. Those which are below [the earth] are the <s>āpas</s> (waters). (AitUp 1.1.2)

children.text: AitUpBh_1,1.2
children.translated_text: [AitUpBh 1,1.2]

children.text:
sa ātmemāṃllokānasṛjata sṛṣṭavān /
yatheha buddhimāṃstakṣādirevaṃprakārānprāsādādīnsṛja iti īkṣitvekṣānantara prāsādādīnsṛjati tadvat /
children.translated_text: He, the Self, created these worlds — brought them into being. Just as here an intelligent craftsman and the like, having deliberated 'I shall create palaces and the like of such-and-such a kind,' creates palaces and the like immediately after deliberation — so too [did the Self].

children.text: nanu sopādānastakṣādiḥ prāsādādīnsṛjatīti yuktaṃ nirupādānastvātmā kathaṃ lokān sṛjati ?
children.translated_text: But [one might object:] it is reasonable that a craftsman, who has material at hand, creates palaces and the like; but the Self, having no material cause, how can He create the worlds?

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ, salilaphenasthānīye ātmabhūte nāmarūpe avyākṛte ātmaikaśabdavācye vyākṛtaphenasthānīyasya /
children.translated_text: This is no defect, for name and form — which occupy the position of water to foam, which are of the nature of the Self, which are unevolved, and which are denoted by the single word 'Self' — serve as the material cause

children.text:
jagataḥ upādānabhūte saṃbhavataḥ /
tasmād ātmabhūtanāmarupopādānabhūtaḥ sansarvajño jagannirmimīta ityaviruddham /
children.translated_text: of the world, which occupies the position of evolved foam. Therefore it is not contradictory that the omniscient one fashioned the universe, having as its material cause name and form that are of the nature of the Self.

children.text:
athavā, yathā vijñānavānmāyāvī nirupādāna ātmānameva ātmāntaratvenākāśena gacchantamiva nirmimīte, tathā sarvajño devaḥ sarvaśaktirmahāmāya ātmānamevātmāntaratvena jagadrūpeṇa nirmimīta iti yuktataram /
evaṃ ca sati kāryakāraṇobhayāsadvādyādipakṣāśca na prasajjante sunirākṛtāśca bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, just as a knowledgeable magician, without any [external] material, projects himself alone as another self appearing to move through the sky, so too the omniscient Lord, the omnipotent great magician, projected Himself alone as another self in the form of the universe — this is even more fitting. And when this is accepted, the doctrines of the unreality of both cause and effect, and other such positions, do not arise, and are thoroughly refuted.

children.text:
kāṃllokānasṛjatetyāha - ambho marīcirmaramāpa iti /
ākāśādikrameṇa aṇḍamutpādyāmbhaḥprabhṛtīn lokānasṛjata /
tatrāmbhaḥprabhṛtīn svayameva vyācaṣṭe śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: What worlds did He create? He says: '<s>ambhas</s>, <s>marīci</s>, <s>mara</s>, and <s>āpas</s>.' Having produced the cosmic egg in the order beginning with space, He created the worlds beginning with <s>ambhas</s>. Among these, the <s>śruti</s> itself explains [the meaning of] <s>ambhas</s> and the rest.

children.text:
adastadambhaḥ śabdavācyo lokaḥ pareṇa divaṃ dyulokātpareṇa parastāt ; so 'mbhaḥśabdavācya ambho bharaṇāt /
dyauḥpratiṣṭhāśrayastasyāmbhaso lokasya /
dyulokādadhastādantarikṣaṃ yattanmarīcayaḥ /
eko 'pyanekasthānabhedatvādbahuvacanabhāk - marīcaya iti ; marīcibhirvā raśmibhiḥsambandhāt /
children.translated_text: Though it is one, because it has many distinct locations it takes the plural — '<s>marīcayaḥ</s>'; or because of its connection with <s>marīcis</s>, that is, rays of light.

children.text: pṛthivī maro mriyante 'smin bhūtānīti /
children.translated_text: The earth is <s>mara</s> — because beings die (<s>mriyante</s>) in it.

children.text: yā adhastāt pṛthivyāstā āpa ucyante ; āpnoteḥ, lokāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those [worlds] which are below the earth are called <s>āpas</s> (waters); from the root āp (to pervade) — [they are] worlds.

children.text: yadyapi pañcabhūtātmakatvaṃ lokānāṃ tathāpyabbāhulyādabnāmabhirevāmbho marīcirmaramāpa ityucyante //2//
children.translated_text: Although the worlds consist of all five elements, nevertheless, because of the predominance of water, they are designated by names of water alone as <s>ambhas</s>, <s>marīci</s>, <s>mara</s>, and <s>āpas</s>. (2)

That [world] yonder, denoted by the word <s>ambhas</s>, is beyond heaven, beyond the celestial world; it is called <s>ambhas</s> because it sustains (<s>bharaṇa</s>). Heaven is the support, the basis, of that world of <s>ambhas</s>. Below the celestial world, the mid-region — that is the <s>marīcis</s>.

children.text: START 1,1.3
children.translated_text: [START 1,1.3]

children.text: sarvaprāṇikarmaphalopādānādhiṣṭhānabhūtāṃścaturo lokān sṛṣṭvā -
children.translated_text: Having created the four worlds, beginning with <s>ambhas</s>, which serve as the substratum and locus for the fruits of the actions of all living beings —

children.text:
sa īkṣateme nu lokāḥ |
lokapālān nu sṛjā iti |
so 'dbhya eva puruṣaṃ samuddhṛtyāmūrcchayat || AitUp_1,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: He deliberated: 'Here now are the worlds. Let me now create world-guardians.' He drew out a person (<s>puruṣa</s>) from the waters and gave him form. (AitUp 1.1.3)

children.text: AitUpBh_1,1.3
children.translated_text: [AitUpBh 1,1.3]

children.text:
sa īśvaraḥ punarevekṣata /
ime nu ambhaḥprabhṛtayo mayā sṛṣṭā lokāḥ paripālayitṛvarjitā vinaśyeyuḥ tasmādeṣāṃ rakṣaṇārthaṃ lokapālāṃllokānāṃ pālayitṛ sṛjai sṛje 'hamiti /
children.translated_text: He, the Lord, deliberated again: 'These worlds beginning with <s>ambhas</s>, created by me, would perish without protectors; therefore, for their protection, let me create <s>lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), guardians of the worlds' — meaning 'I shall create.'

children.text: evamīkṣitvā so 'dbhya evaṃ appradhānebhya eva pañcabhūtebhyo yebhyo 'mbhaḥprabhṛtīnsṛṣṭavāṃstebhya evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, He [drew the <s>puruṣa</s>] from the waters indeed — that is, from the very five elements, in which water predominates, from which He had created [the worlds] beginning with <s>ambhas</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: puruṣaṃ puruṣākāraṃ śiraḥpāṇyādimantaṃ samuddhṛtya adbhyaḥ samupādāya mṛtpiṇḍamiva kulālāḥ pṛthivyāḥ, amūrchayat mūrchitavān saṃpiṇḍitavān svāvayavasaṃyojanenetyarthaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: He drew out a <s>puruṣa</s> — one having the form of a person, possessing head, hands, and other [limbs] — having taken [him] up from the waters, just as potters [take up] a lump of clay from the earth, He gave him form — He compacted him, meaning He joined together his limbs. (3)

children.text: START 1,1.4
children.translated_text: [START 1,1.4]

children.text:
tam abhyatapat |
tasyābhitaptasya mukhaṃ nirabhidyata yathāṇḍam |
mukhād vāk |
vāco 'gniḥ |
nāsike nirabhidyetām |
nāsikābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ |
prāṇād vāyuḥ |
akṣiṇī nirabhidyetām |
akṣībhyāṃ cakṣuḥ |
cakṣuṣa ādityaḥ |
karṇau nirabhidyetām |
karṇābhyāṃ śrotram |
śrotrād diśaḥ |
tvaṅ nirabhidyata |
tvaco lomāni |
lomabhya oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ |
hṛdayaṃ nirabhidyata |
hṛdayān manaḥ |
manasaś candramāḥ |
nābhir nirabhidyata |
nābhyā apānaḥ |
apānān mṛtyuḥ |
śiśnaṃ nirabhidyata |
śiśnād retaḥ |
retasa āpaḥ || AitUp_1,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: He brooded over him. From him, thus brooded upon, the mouth burst open, as an egg does. From the mouth [came forth] speech. From speech, <s>Agni</s> (fire). The nostrils burst open. From the nostrils [came forth] <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). From breath, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind). The eyes burst open. From the eyes [came forth] sight. From sight, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). The ears burst open. From the ears [came forth] hearing. From hearing, the <s>Diśas</s> (quarters). The skin burst open. From the skin [came forth] hairs. From the hairs, herbs and trees. The heart burst open. From the heart [came forth] the mind. From the mind, <s>Candramās</s> (the moon). The navel burst open. From the navel [came forth] <s>apāna</s> (the out-breath). From <s>apāna</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death). The generative organ burst open. From the generative organ [came forth] semen. From semen, the waters. (AitUp 1.1.4)

children.text: AitUpBh_1,1.4
children.translated_text: [AitUpBh 1,1.4]

children.text:
taṃ piṇḍaṃ puruṣavidhamuddiśyābhyatapat /
tadabhidhyānaṃ saṃkalpaṃ kṛtavānityarthaḥ,"yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ"(mu.u.1 / 1 / 9) ityādiśruteḥ /
tasyābhitaptasyeśvarasaṃkalpena tapasābhitaptasya piṇḍasya mukhaṃ nirabhidyata mukhākāraṃ suṣiramajāyata yathā pakṣiṇo 'ṇḍaṃ nirbhidyata evam /
tasmānnirbhinnātmukhādvākkaraṇamindriyaṃ niravartata; tadadhiṣṭhātāgnistato vāco lokapālaḥ /
tathā nāsike nirabhidyetām /
nāsikābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ; prāṇadvāyuḥ; iti sarvatrādhiṣṭhānaṃ karaṇaṃ devatā ca trayaṃ krameṇa nirbhinnamiti /
akṣiṇī karṇau tvag hṛdayamantaḥkaraṇādhiṣṭhānam, mano 'ntaḥkaraṇam : nābhiḥ sarvaprāṇabandhanasthānam /
apānasaṃyuktatvādapāna iti pāyvindriyamucyate /
tasmāt tasyādhiṣṭhātrī devatā mṛtyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, its presiding deity is <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death).

children.text: yathānyatra, tathā śiśnaṃ nirabhidyata prajananendriyasthānam /
children.translated_text: Just as elsewhere, the generative organ burst open — it is the seat of the organ of procreation.

children.text: indriyaṃ reto retovisargārthatvātsaha retasocyate /
children.translated_text: The organ [of procreation] is referred to together with semen as 'semen,' because its purpose is the emission of semen.

children.text: retasa āpa iti //4//
children.translated_text: From semen, the waters. (4)

He brooded over that lump having the form of a person. That means He directed His thought, His <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention), toward it, for the <s>śruti</s> says: 'Whose <s>tapas</s> (austerity) consists of knowledge' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.9). Of that lump, thus brooded upon — that is, heated by the <s>tapas</s> of the Lord's intention — the mouth burst open; a cavity in the shape of a mouth was produced, just as a bird's egg is burst open. From that mouth which had burst open, speech — the organ, the sense faculty — emerged; its presiding deity is <s>Agni</s>, who is thus the <s>lokapāla</s> (world-guardian) of speech. Likewise, the nostrils burst open. From the nostrils, <s>prāṇa</s>; from <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>. In every case, the locus, the organ, and the deity — these three emerged in sequence. The eyes, the ears, the skin — the seat of the inner organ — the heart, the mind as the inner organ, the navel as the binding-place of all the vital breaths. Because of its connection with <s>apāna</s>, the excretory organ is referred to as '<s>apāna</s>.'

children.text: iti prathamādhyāye prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the first chapter. (1)

children.text: START 1,2.1
children.translated_text: [START 1,2.1]

children.text:
tā etā devatāḥ sṛṣṭā asmin mahaty arṇave prāpatan |
tam aśanāpipāsābhyām anvavārjat |
tā enam abruvann āyatanaṃ naḥ prajānīhi |
yasmin pratiṣṭhitā annam adāmeti || AitUp_1,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: These deities, having been created, fell into this great ocean. He subjected him [the <s>puruṣa</s>] to hunger and thirst. They said to Him: 'Find us an abode in which, being established, we may eat food.' (AitUp 1.2.1)

children.text: AitUpBh_1,2.1
children.translated_text: [AitUpBh 1,2.1]

children.text: tā etā agnyādayo devatā lokapālatvena saṃkalpya sṛṣṭā īśvareṇāsminsaṃsārarṇave saṃsārasamudre mahatyavidyākāmakarmaprabhava duḥkhodake tīvrarogajarāmṛtyumahāgrāhe 'nādāvanante 'pāre nirālambe viṣayendriyajanitasukhalavakṣaṇaviśrāme pañcendriyārthatṛṇmārutavikṣobhotthitānarthaśatamahormau mahārauravādyanekanirayagatahāhetyādikūjitākrośanodbhūtamahārave satyārjavadānadayāhiṃsāśamadamadhṛtyādyātmaguṇapātheyapūrṇajñānoḍupe satsaṅgasarvatyāgamārge mokṣatīre etasminmahatyarṇave prāpatanpatitatavatyaḥ /
children.translated_text: These deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others, conceived and created by the Lord as guardians of the worlds, fell into this great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — the sea of transmigration whose waters are the suffering born of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s> (action); whose great sharks are fierce disease, old age, and death; which is beginningless, endless, shoreless, and without support; whose resting places are but the fleeting pleasures born of the senses and their objects; whose hundreds of great waves of calamity are raised by the winds of craving for the five sense-objects; whose great roar arises from the cries of 'alas! alas!' uttered by those fallen into the many hells such as <s>Mahāraurava</s>; in which the raft of knowledge filled with the provisions of <s>ātma-guṇas</s> (virtues of the self) such as truth, uprightness, generosity, compassion, non-violence, tranquility, self-control, and fortitude is the only vessel; whose path is the company of the wise and complete renunciation; and whose far shore is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — into this great ocean they fell.

children.text:
tasmādagnyādidevatāpyayalakṣaṇāpi yā gatirvyākhyātā jñānakarmasamuccayānuṣṭhānaphalabhūtā sāpi nālaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhopaśamāya, ityayaṃ vivakṣitor'the 'tra /
yata evaṃ tasmādevaṃ viditvā paraṃ brahma ātmātmanaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ ca yo vakṣyamāṇaviśeṣaṇaḥ prakṛtaśca jagadutpattisthitisaṃhārahetutvena sa sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhopaśamanāya veditavyaḥ /
tasmāt"eṣa panthā etatkamaitad brahmaitat satyam"(ai.u.2 / 1 / 1) yadetatparabrahmātmajñānam"nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya"(śve.u.3 / 8.6 / 15) iti mantravarṇāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even the destiny described as the dissolution of the deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others, which is the fruit of the combined practice of knowledge and action, is not sufficient for the cessation of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the intended meaning here. Since this is so, therefore, having known thus the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) of oneself and of all beings, which has the characteristics yet to be described, and which is the cause of the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe — that alone is to be known for the cessation of all the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, "This is the path, this is the work, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is the truth" (<s>Aitareya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.1) — this knowledge of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> as the Self — "there is no other path for liberation" (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 3.8, 6.15), as declared by the <s>mantra</s> text.

children.text: taṃ sthānakaraṇadevatotpattibījabhūtaṃ puruṣaṃ prathamotpāditaṃ piṇḍamātmānamaśanāyāpipāsābhyāmanvavārjadanugamitavānsaṃyojitavānityatheḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Puruṣa</s>, the first-created body, who is the seed-cause of the origination of the abodes, organs, and deities — him He joined with, that is, associated and connected with, hunger and thirst.

children.text: tasya kāraṇabhūtasyāśanāyādidoṣavattvāttatkāryabhūtānāmapi devatānāmaśanāyādimattvam /
children.translated_text: Because the causal entity possesses defects such as hunger and the rest, the deities too, being its effects, also possess hunger and the like.

children.text: tāstato 'śanāyāpipāsābhyāṃ pīḍyamānā enaṃ pitāmahaṃ sraṣṭāramabruvannuktavatyaḥ āyatanamadhiṣṭhānaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ prajānīhi vidhatsva /
children.translated_text: They, being afflicted by hunger and thirst, said to him, the Grandfather, the Creator — 'Determine, provide for us an <s>āyatana</s> (abode), a dwelling place,

children.text: yasminnāyatane pratiṣṭhitāḥ samarthāḥ satyo 'nnamadāma bhakṣayāma iti //1//
children.translated_text: established in which abode, being capable, we may eat food, we may consume it.' //1//

children.text: START 1,2.2
children.translated_text: START 1,2.2

children.text: evamukta īśvaraḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the Lord —

children.text:
tābhyo gām ānayat |
tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti |
tābhyo 'śvam ānayat |
tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti || AitUp_1,2.2 ||
children.translated_text:
He brought them a cow.
They said, 'Truly, this is not sufficient for us.'
He brought them a horse.
They said, 'Truly, this is not sufficient for us.' || <s>AitUp</s>_1,2.2 ||

children.text: tābhyo devatābhyo gāṃ gavākṛtiviśiṣṭaṃ piṇḍaṃ tābhya aivādbhyaḥ pūrvavatpiṇḍaṃ samuddhṛtya mūrchayitvānayaddarśitavān /
children.translated_text: For those deities, He brought a cow — a body having the form of a cow — having, as before, drawn out and shaped a body from those same waters, He showed it to them.

children.text: tāḥ punargavākṛtiṃ dṛṣṭavānbruvan - na vai no 'smadarthamadhiṣṭhānāyānnamattumayaṃ piṇḍo 'laṃ na vai /
children.translated_text: They, having seen the cow-form, said — 'Truly, this body is not sufficient for our purpose, as a dwelling place, for eating food.'

children.text: alaṃ paryāptaḥ attuṃ na yogya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Alam</s> means adequate, sufficient; 'not fit to eat' — this is the meaning.

children.text: gavi pratyākhyāte tābhyo 'śvamānayattā abruvanna vai no 'yamalamiti pūrvavat //2//
children.translated_text: The cow having been rejected, He brought them a horse; they said, 'Truly, this is not sufficient for us,' as before. //2//

children.text: START 1,2.3
children.translated_text: START 1,2.3

children.text: sarvapratyākhyāne -
children.translated_text: When all were rejected —

children.text:
tābhyaḥ puruṣam ānayat |
tā abruvan sukṛtaṃ bateti |
puruṣo vāva sukṛtam |
tā abravīd yathāyatanaṃ praviśateti || AitUp_1,2.3 ||
children.translated_text:
He brought them a <s>puruṣa</s> (human form).
They said, 'Well done indeed!'
The <s>puruṣa</s> indeed is well-made.
He said to them, 'Enter according to your respective abodes.' || <s>AitUp</s>_1,2.3 ||

children.text: AitUpBh_1,2.3
children.translated_text: <s>AitUpBh</s>_1,2.3

children.text:
tābhyaḥ puruṣamānayatsvayonibhūtam /
tāḥ svayoniṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā akhinnāḥ satyaḥ sukṛtaṃ śobhanaṃ kṛtamidamadhiṣṭhānaṃ batetyabruvan tasmātpuruṣo vāva puruṣa eva sukṛtaṃ sarvapuṇyakarmahetutvāt /
svayaṃ vā svenevātmanā svamāyābhiḥ kṛtatvātsukṛtamityucyate /
children.translated_text: He brought them a <s>puruṣa</s>, which was their own source. They, seeing the <s>puruṣa</s> as their own source, were delighted and said, '<s>Sukṛtam</s> — well-made, excellently fashioned is this abode indeed!' Therefore, the <s>puruṣa</s> indeed, the human being alone, is <s>sukṛta</s> (well-made), because it is the cause of all meritorious action. Or it is called <s>sukṛta</s> because it is made well by Him, by His own Self, through His own <s>māyā</s> (creative power).

children.text: tā devatā īśvaro 'bravīdiṣṭamāsāmidamadhiṣṭhānamiti matvā sarve hi svayoniṣu ramante, ato yathāyatanaṃ yasya yadvadanādikriyāyogyamāyatanaṃ tatpraviśateti //3//
children.translated_text: The Lord said to those deities, thinking 'This abode is desired by them,' for all beings delight in their own source — therefore, 'Enter according to your respective abodes,' that is, let each enter that abode — such as the mouth and so on — which is suitable for its particular function. //3//

children.text: START 1,2.4
children.translated_text: START 1,2.4

children.text: tathāstvityanujñāṃ pratilabhyeśvarasya nagaryāmiva balādhikṛtādayaḥ -
children.translated_text: Having thus received permission from the Lord, like the commanders of forces and others in a city —

children.text:
agnir vāg bhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśat |
vāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśat |
ādityaś cakṣur bhūtvākṣiṇī prāviśat |
diśaḥ śrotraṃ bhūtvā karṇau prāviśan |
oṣadhivanaspatayo lomāni bhūtvā tvacaṃ prāviśan |
candramā mano bhūtvā hṛdayaṃ prāviśat |
mṛtyur apāno bhūtvā nābhiṃ prāviśat |
āpo reto bhūtvā śiśnaṃ prāviśan || AitUp_1,2.4 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Agni</s>, having become speech, entered the mouth.
<s>Vāyu</s>, having become <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), entered the nostrils.
<s>Āditya</s>, having become sight, entered the eyes.
The <s>Diśas</s> (quarters), having become hearing, entered the ears.
The <s>Oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ</s> (herbs and trees), having become hair, entered the skin.
<s>Candramā</s> (the Moon), having become mind, entered the heart.
<s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), having become <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), entered the navel.
The <s>Āpaḥ</s> (Waters), having become semen, entered the generative organ. || <s>AitUp</s>_1,2.4 ||

children.text: AitUpBh_1,2.4
children.translated_text: <s>AitUpBh</s>_1,2.4

children.text: agnirvāgabhimānī vāgeva bhūtvā svāṃ yoniṃ mukhaṃ prāviśattathoktārthamanyat /
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, the presiding deity of speech, having become speech itself, entered the mouth, his own source; the rest is to be understood similarly as stated.

children.text: vāyurnāsike ādityo 'kṣiṇī diśaḥ karṇau oṣadhivanasyatayastvacaṃ candramā hṛdayaṃ mṛtyurnābhimāpaḥ śiśnaṃ prāviśan //4//
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s> entered the nostrils, <s>Āditya</s> the eyes, the <s>Diśas</s> the ears, the herbs and trees the skin, <s>Candramā</s> the heart, <s>Mṛtyu</s> the navel, and the <s>Āpaḥ</s> entered the generative organ. //4//

children.text: START 1,2.5
children.translated_text: START 1,2.5

children.text: evaṃ labdhādhiṣṭhānāsu devatāsu -
children.translated_text: When the deities had thus obtained their abodes —

children.text:
tam aśanāpipāse abrūtām avābhyām abhiprajānīhīti |
te abravīd etāsv eva vāṃ devatāsv ābhajāmy etāsu bhāginyau karomīti |
tasmād yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havir gṛhyate bhāginyāv evāsyām aśanāpipāse bhavataḥ || AitUp_1,2.5 ||
children.translated_text:
Hunger and thirst said to Him, 'Provide for us two also.'
He said to them, 'I assign you two a share among these very deities; I make you two sharers in them.'
Therefore, for whichever deity an oblation is taken, hunger and thirst become sharers in it. || <s>AitUp</s>_1,2.5 ||

children.text: AitUpBh_1,2.5
children.translated_text: <s>AitUpBh</s>_1,2.5

children.text:
niradhiṣṭhāne satyau aśanāyāpipāse tamīśvaramabrūtāmuktavatyau /
āvābhyāmadhiṣṭhānamabhiprajānīhi cintaya vidhatsvetyarthaḥ /
sa īśvara evamuktaste aśanāyāpipāse abravīt /
na hi yuvayorbhāvarūpatvāccetanāvadvastvanāśrityānnārttṛtvaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, for you two, being of the nature of states, it is not possible to be eaters of food without depending on a conscious entity.'

children.text: tasmādetāsvevāgnyādyāsu vāṃ yuvāṃ devatāsvadhyātmādhidevatāsvābhajāmi vṛttisaṃvibhāgenānugṛhṇāmi /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, I assign you two among these very deities of <s>Agni</s> and the rest, in their <s>adhyātma</s> (individual) and <s>adhidaivata</s> (cosmic) aspects; I favor you by sharing their functions with you.'

children.text: etāsu bhāginyai yaddevatyo yo bhāgo havirādilakṣaṇaḥ syāttasyāstenaiva, bhāgena bhāginyau bhāgavatyau vāṃ karomīti /
children.translated_text: 'I make you two sharers — possessing a share — in these: whatever share, characterized by oblations and the like, belongs to whichever deity, by that very share you two shall partake.'

children.text: sṛṣṭyādāvīśvara evaṃ vyadadhādyasmāttasmādidānīmapi yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai arthāya havirgṛhyate carupuroḍāśādilakṣaṇaṃ bhāginyādeva bhāgavatyāvevāsyāṃ devatāyāmaśanāyapipāse bhavataḥ //5//
children.translated_text: The Lord arranged it thus at the beginning of creation; therefore, even now, for whichever deity and for whatever purpose an oblation is taken — characterized by <s>caru</s> (cooked rice), <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cake), and the like — hunger and thirst, as sharers, possessing a share, exist in that deity. //5//

Being without an abode, hunger and thirst said to that Lord, spoke to Him — 'Provide for us two an abode, think of one, arrange it' — this is the meaning. That Lord, thus addressed, said to hunger and thirst:

children.text: iti prathamādhyāye dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section of the first chapter. //2//

children.text: START 1,3.1
children.translated_text: START 1,3.1

children.text:
sa īkṣateme nu lokāś ca lokapālāś ca |
annam ebhyaḥ sṛjā iti || AitUp_1,3.1 ||
children.translated_text:
He reflected, 'Here now are the worlds and the guardians of the worlds.
Let me create food for them.' || <s>AitUp</s>_1,3.1 ||

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.1
children.translated_text: <s>AitUpBh</s>_1,3.1

children.text: evaṃ hi loke īśvarāṇāmanugrahe nigrahe ca svātantryaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sveṣu /
children.translated_text: For thus in the world it is seen that lords have independence with respect to favoring and punishing their own subjects.

children.text: tadvanmaheśvarasyāpi sarveśvaratvātsarvānprati nigrahānugrahe 'pi svātantryameva //1//
children.translated_text: Likewise, the great Lord too, being the Lord of all, has complete independence with respect to punishing and favoring all beings. //1//

children.text: START 1,3.2
children.translated_text: START 1,3.2

children.text:
so 'po 'bhyatapat |
tābhyo 'bhitaptābhyo mūrtir ajāyata |
yā vai sā mūrtir ajāyatānnaṃ vai tat || AitUp_1,3.2 ||
children.translated_text:
He brooded over the waters.
From those waters, thus brooded upon, a form was born.
That form which was born — that indeed is food. || <s>AitUp</s>_1,3.2 ||

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.2
children.translated_text: <s>AitUpBh</s>_1,3.2

children.text: sa īśaro 'nnaṃ sisṛkṣustā eva pūrvoktā apa uddiśyābhyatapat /
children.translated_text: That Lord, desiring to create food, brooded over those very waters mentioned before.

children.text: tābhyo 'bhitaptābhya upādānabhūtābhyo mūrtirghanarūpaṃ dhāraṇasamartha carācaralakṣaṇamajāyatotpannam /
children.translated_text: From those waters, thus brooded upon, which served as the material cause, a <s>mūrti</s> (form) — a solid substance capable of sustaining, characterized as movable and immovable creation — was born, arose.

children.text: annaṃ vai tanmūrtirūpaṃ yā vai sā mūrtirajāyata //2//
children.translated_text: That form which was born is indeed food — that which has the nature of form. //2//

children.text: START 1,3.3
children.translated_text: START 1,3.3

children.text:
tad enat sṛṣṭaṃ parāṅ atyajighāṃsat |
tad vācājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknod vācā grahītum |
sa yad dhainad vācāgrahaiṣyad abhivyāhṛtya haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.3 ||
children.translated_text:
That food, having been created, sought to flee away.
He tried to grasp it with speech.
He was not able to grasp it with speech.
If he had grasped it with speech, then merely by uttering the name of food one would have been satisfied. || <s>AitUp</s>_1,3.3 ||

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.3
children.translated_text: <s>AitUpBh</s>_1,3.3

children.text: tadenadannaṃ lokalokapālānāmarthe 'bhimukhe sṛṣṭaṃ tadyathā mūṣakādirmārjārādigocare, sanmama mṛtyurannāda iti matvā parāgañcatīti parāṅsadattṝnatītyājighāṃsadatigantumaicchat palāyituṃ prārabhatetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That food, created for the sake of the worlds and the guardians of the worlds, facing them — just as a mouse and the like in the range of a cat and the like — thinking 'Death, the food-eater, is mine,' turned away; that is, it sought to flee, it wished to escape, it began to run away — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadannābhiprāyaṃ matvā sa lokalokapālasaṃghātaḥ kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇaḥ piṇḍaḥ prathamajatvād anyāṃścānnādānapaśyaṃstadannaṃ vācā vadanavyāpāreṇājighṛkṣad grahītumaicchat /
children.translated_text: Understanding the intent of that food, the aggregate of the worlds and guardians of the worlds — the body characterized as the composite of instruments and organs — being the first-born and seeing no other eater of food, tried to grasp that food with speech, that is, through the activity of the mouth, wished to seize it.

children.text: tadannaṃ nāśaknonna samartho 'bhadvācā vadanakriyayā grahītumupādātum /
children.translated_text: He was not able, was not capable, to grasp, to take up, that food with speech, through the activity of the mouth.

children.text: sa prathamajaḥ śarīrī yadyadi hainadvācāgrahaiṣyadgṛhītavānsyādannaṃ sarvo 'pi lokastatkāryabhūtatvādabhivyāhṛtya haivānnamatrapsyattṛpto 'bhaviṣyat, na caitadasti, ato nāśaknodvācā grahītumityavagacchāmaḥ pūrvajo 'pi //3//
children.translated_text: If that first-born embodied being had grasped the food with speech, then everyone in the world, being an effect of that, would have been satisfied by merely uttering the name of food; but this is not the case, and therefore we understand that even the first-born was not able to grasp it with speech. //3//

children.text: samānamuttaram -
children.translated_text: The answer is the same for what follows —

children.text:
tat prāṇenājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknot prāṇena grahītum |
sa yad dhainat prāṇenāgrahaiṣyad abhiprāṇya haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.4 ||
children.translated_text:
He tried to grasp it with <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
He was not able to grasp it with <s>prāṇa</s>.
If he had grasped it with <s>prāṇa</s>, then merely by breathing toward food one would have been satisfied. || <s>AitUp</s>_1,3.4 ||

children.text:
tac cakṣuṣājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknoc cakṣuṣā grahītum |
sa yad dhainac cakṣuṣāgrahaiṣyad dṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.5 ||
children.translated_text:
He tried to grasp it with sight.
He was not able to grasp it with sight.
If he had grasped it with sight, then merely by seeing food one would have been satisfied. || <s>AitUp</s>_1,3.5 ||

children.text:
tac chrotreṇājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknoc chrotreṇa grahītum |
sa yad dhainac chrotreṇāgrahaiṣyac chrutvā haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.6 ||
children.translated_text:
He [the self] tried to grasp it [food] with the ear.
He was unable to grasp it with the ear.
If he had grasped it with the ear, then merely by hearing, one would have been satisfied with food. [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.6]

children.text:
tat tvacājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknot tvacā grahītum |
sa yad dhainat tvacāgrahaiṣyat spṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.7 ||
children.translated_text:
He tried to grasp it with the skin.
He was unable to grasp it with the skin.
If he had grasped it with the skin, then merely by touching, one would have been satisfied with food. [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.7]

children.text:
tan manasājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknon manasā grahītum |
sa yad dhainan manasāgrahaiṣyad dhyātvā haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.8 ||
children.translated_text:
He tried to grasp it with the mind.
He was unable to grasp it with the mind.
If he had grasped it with the mind, then merely by thinking, one would have been satisfied with food. [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.8]

children.text:
tac chiśnenājighṛkṣat |
tan nāśaknoc chiśnena grahītum |
sa yad dhainac chiśnenāgrahaiṣyad visṛjya haivānnam atrapsyat || AitUp_1,3.9 ||
children.translated_text:
He tried to grasp it with the organ of procreation.
He was unable to grasp it with the organ of procreation.
If he had grasped it with the organ of procreation, then merely by emitting, one would have been satisfied with food. [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.9]

children.text:
tad apānenājighṛkṣat |
tad āvayat |
saiṣo 'nnasya graho yad vāyuḥ |
annāyur vā eṣa yad vāyuḥ || AitUp_1,3.10 ||
children.translated_text:
He tried to grasp it with the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath).
He swallowed it.
This grasper of food is <s>Vāyu</s> (the vital air).
This one who lives by food is <s>Vāyu</s>. [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.10]

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.4-10
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 1.3.4-10]

children.text: tatprāṇena taccakṣuṣā tacchrotreṇa tattvacā tanmanasā tacchiśnena tena tena karaṇavyāpāreṇānnaṃ grahītumaśaknuvanpaścādapānena vāyunā mukhacchidreṇa tadannamajighṛkṣat /
children.translated_text: Being unable to grasp the food through the activities of the respective organs — through <s>prāṇa</s> (breathing), through the eye (seeing), through the ear (hearing), through the skin (touching), through the mind (thinking), through the organ of procreation (emitting) — he subsequently tried to grasp that food through the <s>apāna</s> (downward vital air), through the opening of the mouth.

children.text: tadāvayāttadannamevaṃ jagrāha āśitavān /
children.translated_text: He swallowed it — he grasped that food in this manner; he consumed it.

children.text: tena sa eṣo 'pānavāyurannasya graho 'nnagrāhaka ityetat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>apāna</s> (downward vital air) is the grasper of food, the one that grasps food — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadvāyuryo vāyurannāyuḥ annabandhano 'nnajīvano vai prasiddhaḥ sa eṣa yo vāyuḥ //4-10 //
children.translated_text: That which is <s>Vāyu</s> — the <s>Vāyu</s> that is <s>annāyuḥ</s> (living by food), bound to food, sustaining life through food — this indeed is well known. That is this <s>Vāyu</s>. [Commentary on verses 4-10]

children.text: START 1,3.11
children.translated_text: [Start of section 1.3.11]

children.text:
sa īkṣata kathaṃ nv idaṃ mad ṛte syād iti |
sa īkṣata katareṇa prapadyā iti |
sa īkṣata yadi vācābhivyāhṛtaṃ yadi prāṇenābhiprāṇitaṃ yadi cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ yadi śrotreṇa śrutaṃ yadi tvacā spṛṣṭaṃ yadi manasā dhyātaṃ yady apānenābhyapānitaṃ yadi śiśnena visṛṣṭam atha ko 'ham iti || AitUp_1,3.11 ||
children.translated_text:
He reflected: 'How indeed could this exist without me?'
He reflected: 'By which [path] shall I enter?'
He reflected: 'If speaking is done by speech, if breathing is done by <s>prāṇa</s>, if seeing is done by the eye, if hearing is done by the ear, if touching is done by the skin, if thinking is done by the mind, if the downward breathing is done by <s>apāna</s>, if emission is done by the organ of procreation — then who am I?' [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.11]

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.11
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 1.3.11]

children.text:
sa evaṃ lokalokapālasaṃghātasthitimannanimittaṃ kṛtvā purapauratatpālayita sthitisamāṃ svāmīva īkṣata - kathaṃ nu kena prakāreṇeti vitarkayannidaṃ madṛte māmantareṇa purasvāminam, yadidaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātakāya vakṣyamāṇaṃ kathaṃ nu khalu māmantareṇa syātparārthaṃ sat /
yadi vācābhivyāhṛtamityādi kevalameva vāgvyavaharaṇādi tannirarthakaṃ na kathañcana bhavedbalistutyādivat, pauravandyādibhiḥ prayujyamānaṃ svāmyarthaṃ sattatsvāminamantareṇāsatyeva svāmini tadvat /
children.translated_text:
He — having thus created the world, the world-guardians, and established the arrangement of the aggregate [of body and senses] with food as its cause — like an owner of a city who has [created] the city, its citizens, and their protectors, reflected, deliberating 'How, by what means' — this [body-mind complex], without me, that is, without me the owner of the city — this forthcoming aggregate of effects and instruments — how indeed could it exist without me, being something that exists for another's purpose?
'If speaking is done by speech' and so forth — if merely speech and the rest operate by themselves alone, that would be purposeless, just as the praises of <s>Bali</s> [offered by his servants] would be purposeless; being employed by citizens, attendants, and the like, [these activities] exist for the purpose of the master — without the master, when the master does not exist, they would be [purposeless] just like that.

children.text:
tasmānmayā pareṇa svāminādhiṣṭhātrā kṛtākṛtaphalasākṣibhūtena bhoktā bhavitavyaṃ purasyeva rājñā /
yadi nāmaitatsaṃhatakāryasya parārthatvaṃ parārthinaṃ māṃ cetanamantareṇa bhavetpurapaurakāryamiva tatsvāminam, atha ko 'haṃ kiṃsvarūpaḥ kasya vā svāmī?
children.translated_text:
Therefore, there must be a master, a superior, a presiding authority, a witness of what has and has not been accomplished — I must be the experiencer, just as a king is for his city.
If indeed this serving-another-purpose of the aggregate of effects exists without me, the conscious being who is the one seeking that purpose — just as the city-and-citizen activities [exist for] their master — then who am I? Of what nature? And whose master am I?

children.text:
yadyahaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātamanupraviśya vāgādyabhivyāhṛtādiphalaṃ nopalabheya rājeva puramāviśyādhikṛtapuruṣakṛtākṛtāvekṣaṇam na kaścinmāmayaṃ sannevaṃrūpaścetyadhigacchedvicārayet /
viparyaye tu yo 'yaṃ vāgādyabhivyāhṛtādīdamiti veda, sa sanvedanarūpaścetyadhigantavyo 'haṃ syām, yadarthamidaṃ saṃhatānāṃ vāgādīnāmabhivyāhṛtādi, yathā stambhakuḍyādīnāṃ prāsādādisaṃhatānāṃ svāvayavairasaṃhataparārthatvaṃ tadvaditi /
children.translated_text:
If I were to enter this aggregate of effects and instruments and not experience the fruits of speech's utterance and the rest — just as a king who enters a city [but] does not inspect what has and has not been accomplished by the appointed officials — no one would ascertain 'this one, being present, is of such a nature,' [no one] would inquire.
But in the opposite case, he who knows 'this is what has been uttered by speech, etc.' — he, being of the nature of awareness, is to be ascertained as the conscious being — that is what I would be, the one for whose purpose this aggregate of speech and the rest performs its utterance and the like, just as a palace and its constituent parts — pillars, walls, and the like — though their parts are not [independently] aggregated, serve the purpose of another.

children.text: evamīkṣitvātaḥ katareṇa prapadyā iti /
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected — 'then, by which [path] shall I enter?'

children.text: prapadaṃ ca mūrdhā cāsya saṃghātasya praveśamārgau /
children.translated_text: Both the sole of the foot (<s>prapada</s>) and the crown of the head (<s>mūrdhā</s>) are entry paths into this aggregate.

children.text: anayoḥ katareṇa mārgeṇedaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātalakṣaṇaṃ puraṃ prapadyai prapadyeyeti //11//
