children.translated_text: Through which of these two paths should I enter this city characterized as the aggregate of effects and instruments — thus [he reflected]. [Commentary on verse 11]

children.text: START 1,3.12
children.translated_text: [Start of section 1.3.12]

children.text:
evamīkṣitvā na tāvanmadbhṛtyasya prāṇasya mama sarvārthādhikṛtasya praveśamārgeṇa prapadābhyāmadhaḥ prapadye /
kiṃ tarhi pāriśeṣyādasya mūrdhānaṃ vidārya prapadyeyamiti loka ivekṣitakārī -
children.translated_text:
Having thus reflected: 'I shall not first enter through the feet, the entry path of my servant <s>Prāṇa</s> who is appointed to all my affairs.
Rather, by the process of elimination, I shall split open the crown of its head and enter' — like one in the world who acts after deliberation:

children.text:
sa etam eva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata |
saiṣā vidṛtir nāma dvāḥ |
tad etan nāndanam |
tasya traya āvasathās trayaḥ svapnā ayam āvasatho 'yam āvasatho 'yam āvasatha iti || AitUp_1,3.12 ||
children.translated_text:
He split open this very suture (<s>sīman</s>) and entered through this door.
This door is called <s>vidṛti</s> (the opening).
That is the place of bliss (<s>nāndana</s>).
He has three abodes and three dream-states: 'This is an abode, this is an abode, this is an abode.' [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.12]

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.12
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 1.3.12]

children.text:
sa iṣṭeśvara etameva mūrdhasīmānaṃ keśavibhāgāvasānaṃ vidārya cchidrīkṛtvaitayā dvārā mārgeṇemaṃ lokaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātaṃ prāpadyata praviveśa /
seyaṃ hi prasiddhā dvāḥ mūrdhni tailādidhāraṇakāle antastadrasādisaṃvedanāt /
saiṣā vidṛtirvidāritatvādvidṛtirnāma prasiddhā dvāḥ /
children.translated_text:
He, the Lord who has willed [all this], split open this very suture at the crown of the head — the boundary where the parting of the hair ends — having pierced it open, entered through this door, this path, into this world, the aggregate of effects and instruments.
For this is indeed the well-known door at the crown, [known] because at the time of pouring oil and the like, there is internal sensation of its flavor and the rest.
This door, being 'split open' (<s>vidārita</s>), is well known by the name <s>vidṛti</s>.

children.text:
itarāṇi tu śrotrādidvārāṇi bhṛtyādisthānīyasādhāraṇamārgatvānna samṛddhīni nānandahetūni /
idaṃ tu dvāraṃ parameśvarasyaiva kevalasyeti tadetannāndanaṃ nandanameva /
nāndanamiti daidhyaṃ chāndasam nandatyanena dvāreṇa gatvā parasminbrahmaṇīti /
tasyaivaṃ sṛṣṭvā praviṣṭasya jīvenātmanā rājña iva puraṃ traya āvasathāḥ /
jāgaritakāsa indriyasthānaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ cakṣuḥ svapnakāle 'ntarmanaḥ, suṣuptikāle hṛdayākāśa ityetat /
vakṣyamāṇā vā traya āvasthāḥ pitṛśarīraṃ mātṛgarbhāśayaḥ svaṃ ca śarīramiti /
children.translated_text:
The other doors — those of the ear and the rest — are not prosperous, not causes of bliss, because they are common pathways for servants and the like.
But this door belongs exclusively to the Supreme Lord alone — therefore it is <s>nāndana</s>, bliss itself.
<s>Nāndana</s>, with the lengthened vowel, is a Vedic [<s>chāndasa</s>] form; one rejoices (<s>nandati</s>) by going through this door to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
For Him who has thus created [the world] and entered [it] in the form of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) — as a king [enters] a city — there are three abodes:
During the waking state, the seat of the senses, the right eye; during the dream state, the internal mind; during deep sleep, the space within the heart (<s>hṛdayākāśa</s>) — this is the meaning.
Alternatively, the three abodes to be described [later] are: the father's body, the mother's womb, and one's own body.

children.text:
trayaḥ svapnā jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyākhyāḥ /
nanu jāgaritaṃ prabodharūpatvānna svapnaḥ, naivam, svapna eva /
katham? paramārthasvātmaprabodhābhāvātsvapnavadasadvastudarśanācca /
ayamevāvasathaścakṣurdakṣiṇaṃ prathamaḥ, mano 'ntaraṃ dvitīyaḥ, hṛdayākāśastṛtīyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The three dream-states are those called waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
Now, [objection:] 'Waking is not a dream, since it is of the nature of being awake.' Not so — it is indeed a dream.
How? Because there is no awakening to one's own ultimate reality, and because unreal objects are perceived as in a dream.
This first abode is the right eye; the second is the mind within; the third is the space within the heart.

children.text: ayamāvasatha ityuktānukīrtanameva /
children.translated_text: 'This is an abode' — this is merely the repetition of what has been stated.

children.text: teṣu hyayamāvasatheṣu paryāyeṇātmabhāvena vartamāno 'vidyayā dīrghakālaṃ gāḍhaprasuptaḥ svābhāvikyā na prabudhyate 'nekaśatasahasrānarthasaṃnipātajaduḥkhamudgarābhighātānubhavairapi //12//
children.translated_text: For in these abodes, dwelling alternately in the form of the self, deeply asleep through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) for a long time, he does not awaken to his own innate nature — even through the experience of blows from the mallet of suffering produced by the convergence of hundreds of thousands of calamities. [Commentary on verse 12]

children.text: START 1,3.13
children.translated_text: [Start of section 1.3.13]

children.text:
sa jāto bhūtāny abhivyaikhyat kim ihānyaṃ vāvadiṣad iti |
sa etam eva puruṣaṃ brahma tatamam apaśyad idam adarśam itī 3 || AitUp_1,3.13 ||
children.translated_text:
Having been born [i.e., having entered the body], he surveyed the beings: 'Would anyone here wish to declare another [as the self]?'
He beheld this very Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), <s>Brahman</s>, the most pervasive: 'I have seen this!' [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.13]

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.13
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 1.3.13]

children.text: sa jātaḥ śarīre praviṣṭo jīvātmanā bhūtānyabhivyaikhyadvyākarot /
children.translated_text: Having been born — having entered the body — he surveyed, examined the beings in the form of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>).

children.text: sa kadācitparamakāruṇikenācāryeṇātmajñānaprabodhakṛcchabdikāyāṃ vedāntamahāvākyabheryāṃ tatkarṇamūle tāḍyamānāyāmetameva sṛṣṭyādikartṛtvena prakṛtaṃ puruṣaṃ puri śayānamātmānaṃ brahma bṛhattatamaṃ takāreṇaikena luptena tatatamaṃ vyāptatamaṃ paripūrṇamākāśavatpratyabudhyatāpaśyat /
children.translated_text: Then, at some time, through the supreme compassion of a teacher, when the great drum of the <s>Vedānta</s> <s>mahāvākya</s> (great utterance) — belonging to the scriptural tradition of knowledge of the Self — was being beaten at the root of his ear, he directly realized, he beheld, this very Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>) — who had been introduced as the agent of creation and the rest, who sleeps in the city [of the body] — as his own Self, as <s>Brahman</s>, the most expansive (<s>bṛhat-tatama</s>), with the single syllable 'ta' elided, meaning the most pervasive, the most all-pervading, the completely full — like space.

children.text: katham? idaṃ brahma mamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: How [did he see]? 'This — <s>Brahman</s> — of my Self,'

children.text: svarūpamadarśaṃ dṛṣṭavānasmi, aho iti,ṝ.1.3.12vicāraṇārthā plutiḥ pūrvam //13//
children.translated_text: 'I have seen the true nature' — that is, 'I have beheld [it]!' — <s>aho</s> [expressing wonder]. The prolongation [of the vowel] is for the purpose of deliberation. [Commentary on verse 13]

children.text: START 1,3.14
children.translated_text: [Start of section 1.3.14]

children.text: yasmādidamityeva yatsākṣādaparokṣādbrahma sarvāntaramapaśyat parokṣeṇa -
children.translated_text: Because he saw 'this' — that is, because he directly and immediately beheld <s>Brahman</s>, the innermost of all — [He is called <s>Idandra</s>], indirectly [by the name <s>Indra</s>]:

children.text:
tasmād idandro nāma |
idandro ha vai nāma |
tam idandraṃ santam indra ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa |
parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ || AitUp_1,3.14 ||
children.translated_text:
Therefore his name is <s>Idandra</s> ('the seer of this').
<s>Idandra</s> is indeed his name.
Him, who is [truly] <s>Idandra</s>, they call <s>Indra</s> indirectly.
For the gods are fond of the indirect, the gods are fond of the indirect. [<s>AitUp</s> 1.3.14]

children.text: AitUpBh_1,3.14
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 1.3.14]

children.text:
tasmādidaṃ paśyatītīdandro nāma paramātmā /
idandro ha vai nāma prasiddho loka īśvaraḥ /
tamevamidandraṃ santamindra iti parokṣeṇa parokṣābhidhānenācakṣate brahmavidaḥ saṃvyavahārārtham -
children.translated_text:
Therefore, because He sees 'this' (<s>idam</s>), the Supreme Self is named <s>Idandra</s>.
<s>Idandra</s> is indeed his well-known name — the Lord is [so known] in the world.
Him, who is thus <s>Idandra</s>, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> call '<s>Indra</s>' indirectly, by an indirect designation, for the purposes of conventional usage —

children.text: pūjyatamatvātpratyakṣanāmagrahaṇabhayāt /
children.translated_text: Because He is supremely worthy of worship, out of fear of directly pronouncing His [true] name.

children.text: tathā hi parokṣāpriyāḥ parokṣanāmagrahaṇapriyā iva eva hi yasmāddevāḥ, kimuta sarvadevānāmapi devo maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For the gods are fond of the indirect — they are fond of being referred to by indirect names. Since even the gods [are thus], how much more so the God of all gods, the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>)!

children.text: dvivacanaṃ prakṛtādhyāyaparisamāptyartham //14//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the final phrase] is for the purpose of concluding the section under discussion. [Commentary on verse 14]

children.text: iti prathamādhyāye tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the first chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>). [3]

children.text: dvitīya adhyāya
children.translated_text: Second chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>).

children.text: prathama khaṇḍa
children.translated_text: First section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>).

children.text:
asmiṃścaturthe 'dhyāya eṣa vākyārthaḥ - jagadutpattisthitipralayakṛdasaṃsārī sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktiḥ sarvavitsarvamidaṃ jagatsvato 'nyadvastvantaramanupādāyaiva ākāśādikrameṇa sṛṣṭvā svātmaprabodhanārthaṃ sarvāṇi ca prāṇādimaccharīrāṇi svayaṃ praviveśa /
praviśya ca svamātmānaṃ yathāmṛtamidaṃ brahmāsmīti sākṣātpratyabudhyata /
tasmātsa eva sarvaśarīreṣveka evātmā nānya iti /
anyo 'pi"sama ātmā brahmāsmītyevaṃ vidyāt"iti /
"ātmā vā idameka evāgra āsīt"(1 / 1 / 1) iti"brahma tatamam"(1 / 3 / 13) iti coktam /
anyatra ca /
children.translated_text:
In this fourth chapter, the meaning of the passage is this: the omniscient one, possessing all powers, knowing all, who is the agent of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe, and who is free from <s>saṃsāra</s> — He created all this universe, which is other than Himself, without employing any other material, in the sequence beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> (space), and He Himself entered into all the bodies endowed with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest, for the purpose of awakening [beings] to His own Self.
And having entered, He directly realized His own Self: 'I am this immortal <s>Brahman</s>.'
Therefore, He alone is the one Self in all bodies — there is no other.
Another [person] too [should know]: 'The same Self — I am <s>Brahman</s> — one should know thus.'
It has been said: 'The Self alone was this in the beginning, one only' (1.1.1), and '<s>Brahman</s> is all-pervading' (1.3.13).
And elsewhere [as well].

children.text: sarvagatasya sarvātmano bālāgramātramapyapraviṣṭaṃ nāstīti kathaṃ sīmānaṃ vidārya prāpadyata pipīlikeva suṣiram /
children.translated_text: Since nothing, not even the tip of a hair, is un-entered by the all-pervading Self of all, how did He enter by breaking through a boundary, like an ant [entering] a hole?

children.text:
nanvatyalpamidaṃ codyaṃ bahu cātra codayitavyam /
akaraṇaḥ sannīkṣata /
anupādāya kiñcillokānasṛjata /
adbhyaḥ puruṣaṃ samuddhṛtyāmūrchayat /
tasmābhidhyānānmukhādi nirbhinnaṃ mukhādibhyaścāgnyādayo lokapālāsteṣāṃ cāśanāyāpipāsādisaṃyojanaṃ tadāyatanaprārthanaṃ tadarthaṃ gavādipradarśanaṃ teṣāṃ yathāyatanapraveśanaṃ sṛṣṭasyānnasya palāyanaṃ vāgādibhistajjighṛkṣāḥ, etatsarvaṃ sīmāvidāraṇapraveśasamameva /
astu tarhi sarvamevedamanupapannam /
children.translated_text:
Indeed, this objection is a trifling one, and there is much more to be objected to here.
Having no instruments, He deliberated.
Without employing anything, He created the worlds.
From the waters He drew out a person and gave it form.
From His meditation, the mouth and other [openings] burst forth; from the mouth and other [openings], <s>Agni</s> and other world-guardians (<s>lokapālas</s>) [emerged]; the conjunction of hunger, thirst, etc. with them; their seeking an abode; the showing of cows and other [animals] for that purpose; their entry into the respective abodes; the fleeing of the created food; the attempts to seize it through speech and other [faculties] — all of this is exactly like the entry by breaking through a boundary.
Let all of this then be untenable!

children.text:
na, atrātmāvabodhamātrasya vivakṣitatvātsarvo 'yamarthavāda ityadoṣaḥ /
māyāvivadvā mahāmāyāvī devaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktiḥ sarvametaccakāra /
sukhāvabodhanapratipattyarthaṃ lokavadākhyāyikādiprapañca iti yuktataraḥ pakṣaḥ /
na hi sṛṣṭyākhyāyikādiparijñānātkiñcitphalamiṣyate /
aikātmyasvarūpaparijñānāttu amṛtatvaṃ phalaṃ sarvopaniṣatprasiddham /
smṛtiṣu ca gītādyāsu"samaṃsarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram"(gītā 13 / 27) ityādinā /
children.translated_text:
No — because what is intended here is solely the realization of the Self, all this is <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory narrative), and hence there is no fault.
Or, like a magician, the great magician — the divine, omniscient, all-powerful Lord — accomplished all this.
The more reasonable position is that the elaborate narrative-like account is for the purpose of easy comprehension.
For no result is desired from the full understanding of the creation narrative.
But from the full understanding of the essential nature of the unity of the Self, the result — immortality — is well-known in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>.
And in the <s>smṛtis</s> such as the <s>Gītā</s>: 'The Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.27), and so forth.

children.text:
nanu traya ātmānaḥ /
bhoktā kartā saṃsārī jīva ekaḥ sarvalokaśāstraprasiddhaḥ /
anekaprāṇikarmaphalopabhogayogyānekādhiṣṭhānavallokadehanirmāṇena liṅgena yathāśāstrapradarśitena puraprāsādādinirmāṇaliṅgena tadviṣayakauśalajñānavāṃstatkartā takṣādiriveśvaraḥ sarvajño jagataḥ kartā dvitīyaścetana ātmā avagamyate /
"yato vāco nivartante"(tai.u.2 / 4 / 1) "neti neti"(bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 23) ityādiśāstraprasiddha aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣastṛtīyaḥ evamete traya ātmānānyonyavilakṣaṇāḥ tatra kathameka eva ātmā advitīyaḥ asaṃsārīti jñātuṃ śakyate?
children.translated_text:
But there are three selves!
The first is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — the enjoyer, agent, and transmigrating being — well-known in all the world and in scripture.
A second conscious self — <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the omniscient maker of the universe — is understood [from the inference that] one who creates manifold abode-like worlds and bodies suitable for the experience of the fruits of the actions of many living beings must possess, as an inferential mark, knowledge and skill in that [creation], just like a carpenter and the like who are known by the inferential mark of constructing cities, palaces, etc.
The third is the <s>Aupaniṣada Puruṣa</s> (the Person of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>), well-known from scriptural [texts] such as 'From which words turn back' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.1) and '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.23). These three selves being mutually distinct, how can it be known that the Self is one alone, without a second, and free from <s>saṃsāra</s>?

children.text: tatra jīva eva tāvatkathaṃ jñāyate?
children.translated_text: Among these, how is the <s>jīva</s> first known?

children.text: nanvevaṃ jñāyate śrotā mantā draṣṭā ādeṣṭā āghoṣṭā vijñātā prajñāteti /
children.translated_text: It is known thus: as hearer, thinker, seer, commander, speaker, knower, discerner.

children.text:
nanu vipratiṣiddhaṃ jñāyate yaḥ śravaṇādikartṛtvenāmato mantāvijñāto vijñāteti ca /
tathā"na matermantāraṃ manvīthā na vijñātevijñātāraṃ vijānīyāḥ"(bṛ.u.3 / 4 / 2) ityādi ca /
children.translated_text:
But contradictory things are known — it is inferred as the agent of hearing, etc., that it is the thinker and the knower, and yet also [it is said that it is] not known.
And also: 'You should not think of the thinker of thought; you should not know the knower of knowledge' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.4.2), etc.

children.text:
satyaṃ vipratiṣiddham, yadi pratyakṣeṇa jñāyeta sukhādivat /
pratyakṣajñānaṃ ca nivāryate"na matermantāraṃ manvīthāḥ"(bṛ.u.3 / 3 / 2) ityādinā /
jñāyate tu śravaṇādiliṅgena, tatra kuto vipratiṣedhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
True, [it would be] contradictory if it were known through direct perception, like pleasure and the like.
But direct perceptual knowledge is precluded by [texts] such as 'You should not think of the thinker of thought' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.3.2), etc.
But [the Self] is known through inferential marks such as hearing, etc. — where then is the contradiction?

children.text:
nanu śravaṇādiliṅgenāpi kathaṃ jñāyate? yāvatā yadā śṛṇotyātmā śrotavyaṃ śabdaṃ tadā tasya śravaṇakriyayaiva vartamānatvānmananavijñānakriye na saṃbhavataḥ ātmani paratra vā /
tathānyatrāpi mananādikriyāsu /
śravaṇādikriyāśca svaviṣayeṣveva /
na hi mantavyādanyatra manturmananakriyā saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text:
But how is it known even through inferential marks such as hearing? Insofar as when the Self hears, being engaged in the very activity of hearing the audible sound, the activities of thinking and discerning are not possible — either in the Self or elsewhere.
Likewise in the other activities such as thinking, etc.
And the activities of hearing, etc. are only with respect to their own objects.
For the activity of thinking by the thinker is not possible with respect to anything other than the thinkable.

children.text: nanu manasā sarvameva mantavyam /
children.translated_text: But everything is thinkable by the mind!

children.text: satyamevaṃ tathāpi sarvamapi mantavyaṃ mantāramantareṇa na mantuṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: True, even so, everything that is thinkable cannot be thought without [there being] a thinker.

children.text: yadyevaṃ kiṃ syāt?
children.translated_text: If so, what would follow?

children.text:
idamatra syāt, sarvasya yo 'yaṃ mantā sa mantaiveti na sa mantavyaḥ syāt /
na ca dvitīyo manturmantāsti /
yadā sa ātmanaiva mantavyastadā yena ca mantavyaḥ ātmā ātmanā yaśca mantavya ātmā tau dvau prasajyeyātām /
eka evātmā dvidhā mantṛmantavyatvena dviśakalībhavedvaṃśādivat ubhayathāpyanupapattireva /
yathā pradīpayoḥ prakāśyaprakāśakatvānupapattiḥ samatvāttadvat /
children.translated_text:
This would follow here: he who is the thinker of everything is the thinker alone — he cannot be the thinkable.
And there is no second thinker of the thinker.
If the Self were to be thought by Itself, then two [selves] would be entailed — that by which the Self is to be thought, and the Self that is to be thought.
Or one single Self would split in two — as thinker and thinkable — like a bamboo [split in two]. In either case there is nothing but impossibility.
Just as mutual illumination between two lamps is impossible because of their equality — so it is here.

children.text:
na ca manturmantavye mananavyāpāraśūnyaḥ kālo 'styātmamananāya /
yadāpi liṅgenātmānaṃ manute mantāḥ, tadāpi pūrvavadeva liṅgena mantavya ātmā yaśca tasya mantā tau dvau prasajyeyātām /
eka eva vā dvidheti pūrvoktadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
And there is no time when the thinker, being void of the activity of thinking with respect to the thinkable, could think the Self.
Even when one thinks the Self through an inferential mark — even then, as before, two would be entailed: the Self that is to be thought through the mark, and the one who is its thinker.
Or the one [Self] would [split] in two — the same defect as stated before.

children.text: na pratyakṣeṇa nāpyanumānena jñāyate cet kathamucyate"sa ma ātmeti vidyāt"(kauṣī.3 / 9) iti? kathaṃ vā śrotā mantetyādi?
children.translated_text: If [the Self] is known neither by direct perception nor by inference, how is it said 'One should know: He is my Self' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 3.9)? And how [is it said] 'hearer, thinker,' etc.?

children.text:
nanu śrotṛtvādidharmavānātmā aśrotṛtvādi ca prasiddhamātmanaḥ /
kimatra viṣamaṃ paśyasi?
children.translated_text:
Well, the Self is known to possess properties such as hearing, etc., and the absence of hearing, etc. is also well-known of the Self.
What difficulty do you see here?

children.text:
yadyapi tava na viṣamaṃ tathāpi mama tu viṣamaṃ pratibhāti /
katham? yadāsau śrotā tadā na mantā yadā mantā tadā na śrotā /
tatraivaṃ sati pakṣe śrotā mantā pakṣe na śrotā nāpi mantā /
tathānyatrāpi ca /
children.translated_text:
Even if there is no difficulty for you, still a difficulty appears to me.
How so? When it is a hearer, it is not a thinker; when it is a thinker, it is not a hearer.
That being the case, alternatively it is a hearer and a thinker, alternatively it is neither a hearer nor a thinker.
And likewise in other cases too.

children.text:
yadaivaṃ tadā śrotṛtvādidharmavānātmā aśrotṛtvādidharmavānveti saṃśayasthāne kathaṃ tava na vaiṣamyam /
yadā devadatto gacchati tadā na sthātā gantaiva /
yadā tiṣṭhati tadā na gantā sthātaiva /
tadā asya pakṣa eva gantṛtvaṃ sthātṛtvaṃ ca /
na nityaṃ gantṛtvaṃ sthātṛtvaṃ vā /
tadvat /
children.translated_text:
If that is so, then at the point of doubt whether the Self possesses properties such as hearing or properties such as non-hearing, how is there no difficulty for you?
When <s>Devadatta</s> walks, he is not a stander — he is a walker only.
When he stands, he is not a walker — he is a stander only.
Then his walkerhood and standerhood are only occasional.
Neither walkerhood nor standerhood is permanent.
Just so [with the Self's hearing, etc.].

children.text:
tathaivātra kāṇādādayaḥ paśyanti /
pakṣaprāptenaiva śrotṛtvādinā ātmocyate śrotā mantetyādivacanāt /
saṃyogajatvamayaugapadyaṃ ca jñānasya hyācakṣate /
darśayanti cānyatramanā /
abhūvaṃ nādarśamityādi yugapajjñānānupattirmanaso liṅgamiti ca nyāyyam /
bhavatvevam kiṃ tava naṣṭaṃ yadyevaṃ syāt?
astvevaṃ taveṣṭaṃ cet /
śrutyarthastu na saṃbhavati /
kiṃ na śrotā mantetyādiśrutyathaḥ
na, na śrotā na mantetyādivacanāt /
nanu pākṣikatvena pratyuktaṃ tvayā /
na, nityameva śrotṛtvādyabhyupagamāt /
"na hi śrotuḥ śruterviparilopo vidyate"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 27) ityādiśruteḥ /
evaṃ tarhi nityameva śrotṛtvādyabhyupagame pratyakṣaviruddhā yugapajjñānotpattirajñānābhāvāvaścātmanaḥ kalpitaḥ syāt /
taccāniṣṭamiti /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Kāṇādas</s> (followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s>) and others view it in exactly this way.
The Self is spoken of as 'hearer, thinker,' etc. because of hearing, etc. that are only occasionally obtained — based on the [Upaniṣadic] statements.
They declare that cognition is produced by conjunction [of Self and mind] and is non-simultaneous.
And they show [this from experience]: 'My mind was elsewhere; I did not see' — the non-occurrence of simultaneous cognitions is an inferential mark for [the involvement of] the mind. This is reasonable.
Let it be so — what have you lost if it is thus?
Let it be as you wish.
But the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is not possible [on your view].
How? Is not 'hearer, thinker,' etc. the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>?
No — because of the statement 'not a hearer, not a thinker,' etc. [as well].
But you replied [to that] with the [claim of] occasional character.
No — because eternal hearing, etc. is accepted [by the <s>śruti</s>].
From the <s>śruti</s>: 'For the hearer, there is no cessation of hearing' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.27), etc.
If so, then by accepting eternal hearing, etc., the arising of simultaneous cognitions — which contradicts perception — and the absence of ignorance in the Self would be fabricated.
And that is undesirable — thus [the opponent's position is refuted].

children.text:
nobhayadoṣopapattiḥ /
ātmanaḥ śrutyādiśrotṛtvādidharmavattvaśruteḥ /
anityānāṃ mūrtānāṃ ca cakṣurādīnāṃ dṛṣṭyādyanityameva saṃyogaviyogadharmiṇām, yathāgnerjvalanaṃ tṛṇādisaṃyogajatvāttadvat /
na tu nityasyāmūrtasyāsaṃyogaviyogadharmiṇaḥ saṃyogajadṛṣṭyādyanityadharmavattvaṃ saṃbhavati /
tathā ca śrutiḥ"na hi draṣṭurdṛṣṭerviparilopo vidyate"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) ityādyā /
evaṃ tarhi dve dṛṣṭī cakṣuṣo 'nityādṛṣṭirnityā cātmanaḥ /
tathā ca dve śrutī śrotrasyānityā nityā cātmasvarūpasya /
tathā dve matī vijñātī bāhyābāhye evaṃ hyeva /
tathā ceyaṃ śrutirupapannā bhavati"dṛṣṭerdraṣṭā śruteḥ śrotā"ityādyā /
children.translated_text:
Neither of the two faults applies [to our position].
Because the <s>śruti</s> teaches that the Self possesses properties such as hearing, etc.
For the impermanent, material [organs] such as the eye, etc. — which are subject to conjunction and disjunction — sight and the like are impermanent, just as the burning of fire is [impermanent] because it is produced by conjunction with grass and the like.
But for [the Self], which is eternal, immaterial, and not subject to conjunction and disjunction, the possession of impermanent properties such as sight produced by conjunction is not possible.
And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'For the seer, there is no cessation of sight' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23), etc.
If so, then there are two [kinds of] sight: the impermanent [sight] of the eye, and the eternal [sight] of the Self.
Likewise, there are two [kinds of] hearing: the impermanent [hearing] of the ear, and the eternal [hearing] belonging to the essential nature of the Self.
Likewise, there are two [kinds of] thought and cognition — external and internal. Indeed, it is just so.
And thus this <s>śruti</s> is justified: 'The seer of sight, the hearer of hearing,' etc.

children.text:
loko 'pi prasiddhaṃ cakṣuṣastimirāgamāpāyayornaṣṭā dṛṣṭirjātā dṛṣṭiriti cakṣurdṛṣṭeranityatvam tathā ca śrutimatyādīnāmātmadṛṣṭyādīnāṃ ca nityatvaṃ prasiddhameva loke /
vadati hi uddhṛtacakṣuḥ svapne 'dyamayā bhrātā dṛṣṭa iti /
tathāvagatabādhiryaḥ svapneśruto mantro 'dyetyādi /
yadi cakṣuḥsaṃyogajaivātmano nityā dṛṣṭistannāśo naśyet /
tadoddhṛtacakṣuḥ svapne nīlapītādi na paśyet /
"na hi draṣṭurdṛṣṭeḥ"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) ityādyā ca śrutiranupapannā syāt /
"taccakṣuḥ puruṣo yena svapne paśyati"ityādyā ca śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text:
In common experience too, it is well known that the impermanence of the eye's sight [is seen] from the coming and going of eye-diseases such as <s>timira</s> (cataract): 'Sight was lost, sight has arisen.' And likewise, the eternality of the intelligent person's own vision (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and the like is well known in the world.
For one whose eyes have been removed says in a dream: 'Today my brother was seen by me.'
Likewise, one who has become deaf [says] in a dream: 'Today a <s>mantra</s> was heard,' and so forth.
If the Self's eternal sight were produced only by conjunction with the eye, it would perish when that [conjunction] is destroyed.
Then one whose eyes have been removed would not see blue, yellow, etc. in a dream.
And the <s>śruti</s> such as 'For the seer, there is no cessation of sight' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23) would be untenable.
As also the <s>śruti</s>: 'The Person by which one sees in a dream is that [faculty of] sight' and the like.

children.text:
nityā ātmano dṛṣṭirbāhyānityadṛṣṭergrāhikā /
bāhyadṛṣṭeścopajanāpāyādyānityadharmavattvāttadgrāhikāyā ātmadṛṣṭestadvadavabhāsatvamanityatvādi bhrāntinimittaṃ lokasyeti yuktam /
yathā bhramaṇādidharmavadalātādivastuviṣayadṛṣṭirapi bhramatīva tadvat /
tathā ca śrutiḥ"dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 7) iti /
tasmādātmadṛṣṭernityatvānna yaugapadyamayaugapadyaṃ vāsti /
children.translated_text:
The Self's sight is eternal and is the grasper of the external, impermanent sight.
And since the external sight has impermanent properties such as arising and ceasing, it is reasonable that the Self's sight, which grasps it, appears as if it too possesses those [impermanent properties] — and this is the cause of the world's delusion regarding impermanence, etc.
Just as the sight directed toward objects such as a firebrand and the like, which possess properties such as rotation, appears as if it too rotates — so it is here.
And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'As if thinking, as if moving' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.7).
Therefore, since the Self's sight is eternal, there is neither simultaneity nor non-simultaneity [as a problem].

children.text:
bāhyānityadṛṣṭyupādhivaśāttu lokasya tārkikāṇāṃ cāgamasaṃpradāyavarjitatvād anityā ātmano dṛṣṭiriti bhrāntirupapannaiva /
jīveśvaraparamātmabhedakalpanā caitannimittaiva /
tathā ca asti nāstītyādyāśca yāvanto vāṅmanasayorbhedā yatraikaṃ bhavanti, tadviṣayāyā nityāyā dṛṣṭernirviśeṣāyāḥ asti nāsti, ekaṃ nānā, guṇavadaguṇam, jānāti na jānāti, kriyāvadakriyam phalavadaphalam, sabījaṃ nirbījam, sukhaṃ duḥkham, madhyamamadhyam, śūnyamaśūnyam, paro 'hamanya iti vā saravavākpratyayāgocare svarūpe yo vikalpayitumicchati, sa nūnaṃ khamati carmavadveṣṭayitumicchati, sopānamiva ca padbhyāmāroḍhum jale khe ca mīnānāṃ vayasāṃ ca padaṃ didṛkṣate /
"neti neti"(bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 23) "yato vāco nivartante"(tai.u.2 / 4 / 1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
"ko addhā veda"(ṛ.saṃ.1 / 3 / 6) ityādimantravarṇāt /
kathaṃ tarhi tasya sa ma ātmeti vedanam /
brūhi kena prakāreṇa tamahaṃ sa ma ātmeti vidyām /
children.translated_text:
But due to the conditioning (<s>upādhi</s>) of the external, impermanent sight, the delusion of the world and of the logicians (<s>tārkikas</s>) — who are devoid of the tradition of scripture — that the Self's sight is impermanent, is indeed well-established.
And the imagining of distinctions among the individual self (<s>jīva</s>), the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), and the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) has this very [delusion] as its cause.
And thus — 'It exists,' 'It does not exist' — and as many distinctions of speech and mind as there are, where they all become one — whoever wishes to determine the essential nature of that eternal, undifferentiated sight, which has as its object [that which is] beyond all distinctions of 'exists' and 'does not exist,' 'one' and 'many,' 'with qualities' and 'without qualities,' 'knows' and 'does not know,' 'with activity' and 'without activity,' 'with result' and 'without result,' 'with seed' and 'without seed,' 'happy' and 'unhappy,' 'intermediate' and 'non-intermediate,' 'void' and 'non-void,' 'supreme' and 'I' and 'another' — beyond the reach of all words and concepts — that person surely wishes to roll up space like a piece of leather, or to climb the sky on foot like a staircase, and seeks to find the tracks of fish and birds in the water and sky!
From the <s>śrutis</s>: '<s>Neti neti</s> (not this, not this)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.23), 'From which words turn back' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.1), and the like.
From the <s>mantra</s> passages such as 'Who indeed truly knows?' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 10.129.6).
Then how is there the knowledge 'He is my Self'?
Tell me: by what means would I know 'He is my Self'?

children.text:
atrākhyāyikāmācakṣate - kaścitkila manuṣyo mugdhaḥ kaiściduktaḥ kasmiṃścidaparādhe sati dhiktvāṃ nāsi manuṣya iti /
sa mugdhatayā ātmano manuṣyatvaṃ pratyāyayituṃ kañcidupetyāha bravītu bhavānko 'hamasmīti /
sa tasya mugdhatāṃ jñātvāha /
krameṇa bodhayiṣyāmīti /
sthāvarādyātmabhāvamapohya na tvamamanuṣya ityuktvopararāma /
sa taṃ mugdhaḥ pratyāha bhavānmāṃ bodhayituṃ pravṛttastūṣṇīṃ babhūva /
kiṃ na bodhayatīti? tādṛgeva tadbhavito vacanam /
nāsyamanuṣya ityukte 'pi manuṣyatvamātmano na pratipadyate yaḥ sa kathaṃ manuṣyo 'sītyukto 'pi manuṣyatvamātmanaḥ pratipadyeta tasmādyathāśāstropadeśa evātmāvabodhavidhirnānyaḥ /
na hyagnerdāhyaṃ tṛṇādyanyena kenaciddgdhuṃ śakyam /
ata eva śāstramātmasvarūpaṃ bodhayituṃ pravṛttaṃ sadamanuṣyatvapratiṣedheneva"neti neti"
children.translated_text:
Here they relate an illustrative story: A certain man, it is said, was confused. When he had committed some offense, some people said to him, rebuking him: 'Fie on you! You are not a [real] man!' He, being confused, approached someone in order to have his humanness confirmed, and said: 'Sir, please tell me — who am I?' The other, recognizing his confusion, said: 'I shall instruct you gradually.' Having removed the idea of being a plant and such, he said 'You are not a non-human' and stopped.
The confused man replied: 'Sir, you have undertaken to instruct me, but you have fallen silent — why do you not instruct me?' The response is of precisely that nature.
One who, even when told 'You are not a non-human,' does not recognize his own humanness — how would he recognize his humanness when told 'You are a human'? Therefore, just as is the teaching of scripture, so is the method of Self-realization — there is no other.
For the combustible material of fire — grass and the like — cannot be burned by anything other [than fire].
For precisely this reason, scripture, having undertaken to teach the essential nature of the Self, speaks — just as [in the story] by the mere negation of non-humanness — saying '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this)

children.text:
(bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 23) ityuktvopararāma /
tathā"ananta ramabāhyam"(bṛ.u.2 / 5 / 19, 3 / 8 / 8) "ayamātmā brahma sarvānubhūḥ"(bṛ.u.2 / 5 -19) ityanuśāsanam /
"tattvamasi"(chā.u.3 / 8 / 16) "yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14, 4 / 5 / 15) ityevamādyapi ca /
children.translated_text:
(<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.23), and stops.
Likewise the instruction: 'Infinite, without external [attributes]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.19; 3.8.8), 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>, the experience of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.19).
'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.7), 'When for him everything has become the Self alone — then by what and whom would he see?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14; 4.5.15) — and so forth as well.

children.text:
yāvadayamevaṃ yathoktamimamātmānaṃ na vetti tāvadayaṃ bāhyānityadṛṣṭilakṣaṇamupādhimātmatvenopetya avidyayā upādhidharmānātmano manyamāno brahmādistambaparyanteṣu devatiryaṅnarasthāneṣu punaḥ punarāvartamāno 'vidyākāmakarmavaśātsaṃsarati /
sa evaṃ punarevameva nadīsrotovajjanmamaraṇaprabandhāvicchedena vartamānaḥ kābhiravasthābhirvartata ityetamarthaṃ darśayantyāha śrutirvairāgyahetoḥ -
children.translated_text:
As long as this [self] does not know this Self as described — so long does it, having adopted the conditioning (<s>upādhi</s>) characterized by the external, impermanent sight as its own self through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), imagining the properties of the conditioning to belong to the Self, transmigrate through the stations of gods, animals, and humans — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — revolving again and again under the power of <s>avidyā</s>, desire, and <s>karma</s>.
Thus revolving continuously like a river's current in the unbroken succession of birth and death — in what states does it exist? Showing this meaning, the <s>śruti</s> speaks, for the purpose of producing dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>):

children.text: START 2.1
children.translated_text: [Start of section 2.1]

children.text:
puruṣe ha vā ayam ādito garbho bhavati yad etad retaḥ |
tad etat sarvebhyo 'ṅgebhyas tejaḥ sambhūtam ātmany evātmānaṃ bibharti |
tad yadā striyāṃ siñcaty athainaj janayati |
tad asya prathamaṃ janma || AitUp_2.1 ||
children.translated_text:
In a man, this [self] first becomes an embryo — that which is this semen.
This is the essence (<s>tejas</s>) collected from all the limbs; he bears the self within the self.
When he deposits it in a woman, then he begets it.
That is his first birth. [<s>AitUp</s> 2.1]

children.text: AitUpBh_2.1
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 2.1]

children.text:
ayamevāvidyākāmakarmābhimānavān yajñādikarma kṛtvāsmāllokād dhūmādikrameṇa annabhūtaḥ puruṣāgnau hutaḥ /
tasminpuruṣe ha vā ayaṃ saṃsārī rasādikrameṇa āditaḥ prathamato retorūpeṇa garbho bhavatītyetadāha yadetatpuruṣe retastena rūpeṇeti /
taccaitadreto 'nnamayasya piṇḍasya sarvebhyo 'ṅgebhyo 'vayavebhyo rasādilakṣaṇebhyastejaḥ sārarūpaṃ śarīrasya saṃbhūtaṃ pariniṣpannaṃ tatpuruṣasyātmabhūtatvādātmā /
tamātmānaṃ retorūpeṇa garbhībhūtamātmanyeva svaśarīra evātmānaṃ bibharti dhārayati /
children.translated_text:
This very [self], possessing the false identification with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s>, having performed sacrificial rites and the like, departing from this world through the path of smoke and the rest, having become food, is offered into the fire of a man.
In that man, this transmigrating being first — that is, initially — becomes an embryo in the form of semen, through the sequence of food-essence and the rest. This is what [the text] says: 'that which is this semen in a man' — meaning 'in that form.' And this semen — the essence (<s>tejas</s>), the quintessence of the body — has arisen, has been produced, from all the limbs, from all the parts characterized by food-essence and the like, of the food-based bodily aggregate. Since it has become the self of the man, it is [called] the self. He bears that self, which has become an embryo in the form of semen, within the self — that is, within his own body; he sustains it.

children.text: tadreto yadā yasminkāle bhāryartumatī tasyāṃ yoṣāgnau striyā siñcatyugacchan, atha tadainadetadreta ātmano garbhabhūtaṃ janayati pitā /
children.translated_text: That semen — at the time when the wife is in her fertile period — he deposits it, he discharges it, in that woman, in the fire of the womb. Then at that time, this semen, which has become the embryo of his self, is begotten by the father.

children.text: tadasya puruṣasya sthānānnirgamanaṃ retaḥsekakāle retorūreṇāsya saṃsāriṇaḥ prathamaṃ janma prathamāvasthābhivyaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: That departure from his station — at the time of the depositing of semen — in the form of semen, is the first birth of this transmigrating being, the first manifestation of [this] state.

children.text: tadetaduktaṃ purastāt"asāvātmāmumātmānam"ityādinā //1//
children.translated_text: This has been stated earlier with 'this self [is placed in] that self' and so forth. [Commentary on verse 1]

children.text: START 2.2
children.translated_text: [Start of section 2.2]

children.text:
tat striyā ātmabhūyaṃ gacchati yathā svam aṅgaṃ tathā |
tasmād enāṃ na hinasti |
sāsyaitam ātmānam atra gataṃ bhāvayati || AitUp_2.2 ||
children.translated_text:
It [the embryo] becomes one with the woman's self, as if it were her own limb.
Therefore it does not harm her.
She nourishes this self of his that has come into her. [<s>AitUp</s> 2.2]

children.text: AitUpBh_2.2
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 2.2]

children.text:
tadreto yasyāṃ striyāṃ siktaṃ sattasyā ātmabhūyamātmāvyatirekatāṃ yathā piturevaṃ gacchati prāpnoti yathā svamaṅgaṃ stanādi tathā tadvadeva /
tasmāddhetorenāṃ mātaraṃ sa garbho na hinasti piṭakādivat /
yasmātstanādi svāṅgavadātmabhūtaṃ gataṃ tasmānna hinasti na bādhata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
That semen, deposited in whichever woman, attains the state of being one with the self of that woman — non-separateness from her — just as [it was] with the father, becoming like her own limb such as the breast and the like.
For that reason, that embryo does not harm the mother, like a boil [would]. Since it has become one with the self, like a breast and other limbs, therefore it does not harm — it does not injure: this is the meaning.

children.text: sā antarvatnyetamasya bharturātmānamatrātmana udare gataṃ praviṣṭaṃ buddhvā bhāvayati vardhayati paripālayati garbhaviruddhāśanādiparihāramanukūlāśanādyupayogaṃ ca kurvatī //2//
children.translated_text: She, being pregnant, knowing that this self of her husband has entered here, into her womb, nourishes it, cultivates it, tends to it — by avoiding food and other things harmful to the embryo and by taking food and other things conducive [to its health]. [Commentary on verse 2]

children.text: START 2.3
children.translated_text: [Start of section 2.3]

children.text:
sā bhāvayitrī bhāvayitavyā bhavati |
taṃ strī garbhaṃ bibharti |
so 'gra eva kumāraṃ janmano 'gre 'dhi bhāvayati |
sa yat kumāraṃ janmano 'gre 'dhi bhāvayaty ātmānam eva tad bhāvayaty eṣāṃ lokānāṃ santatyai |
evaṃ santatā hīme lokāḥ |
tad asya dvitīyaṃ janma || AitUp_2.3 ||
children.translated_text:
She who nourishes is to be nourished [in return].
The woman bears the embryo.
He [the father] cherishes the child even before birth.
In that he cherishes the child before birth, he cherishes the Self itself, for the continuation of these worlds.
For thus are these worlds continued.
That is his second birth. [<s>AitUp</s> 2.3]

children.text: AitUpBh_2.3
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 2.3]

children.text:
sā bhāvayitrī vardhayitrī bharturātmano garbhabhūtasya bhāvayitavyā vardhayitavyā rakṣayitavyā ca bhartā bhavati /
na hyupakārapratyupakāramantareṇa loke kasyacitkenacitsambandha upapadyate /
taṃ garbhaṃ strī yathoktena garbhadhāraṇavidhānena bibharti dhārayatyagre prāgjanmanaḥ /
sa pitā agra eva pūrvameva jātamātraṃ janmano 'dhyūrdhvaṃ janmano jātaṃ kumāraṃ jātakarmādinā pitā bhāvayati /
sa pitā yadyasmātkumāraṃ janmano 'dhyūrdhvamagre jātamātrameva jātakarmādinā yadbhāvayati /
tadātmānameva bhāvayati /
piturātmaiva hi putrarūpeṇa jāyate /
tathā hyuktam"patirjāyāṃ praviśati"(hari.3 / 73 / 31) ityādi /
children.translated_text:
She who nourishes — who cultivates the embryo that has become the husband's self — is to be nourished, cultivated, and protected by the husband.
For in the world, no relationship between anyone and anyone is possible without mutual exchange of benefit.
The woman bears that embryo through the prescribed procedures for maintaining pregnancy, before — that is, prior to — the birth. The father cherishes — before the very [moment of] birth, from the very moment of birth — the child, the newborn, through the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth-rites) and the like. The father cherishes the child because — since he cherishes the child, the newborn, through the <s>jātakarma</s> and the like from the very moment of birth — he thereby cherishes the Self itself. For the father's self is indeed born in the form of the son. As it has been said: 'The husband enters the wife' (<s>Harivaṃśa</s> 3.73.31) and so forth.

children.text: tatkimarthamātmānaṃ putrarūpeṇa janayitvā bhāvayatītyucyate - eṣāṃ lokānāṃ santatyā avicchedāyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For what purpose does he beget himself in the form of a son and nourish [him]? It is said: for the continuation of these worlds — meaning, for their non-interruption.

children.text: vicchidyeranhīme lokāḥ putrotpādanādi yadi na kuryuḥ kecana /
children.translated_text: For these worlds would be interrupted if no one were to perform the production of sons and the like.

children.text: evaṃ putrotpādanādikarmāvicchedenaiva santatāḥ prabandharūpeṇa vartante hi yasmādime lokāstasmāttadavicchedāya tatkartavyaṃ na mokṣāyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, these worlds continue in the form of an unbroken series, through the very uninterruptedness of actions such as the begetting of sons and the like. Therefore, for the sake of their continuity, those [actions] are to be performed — not for the sake of liberation. That is the meaning.

children.text: tadasya saṃsāriṇaḥ kumārarūpeṇa māturudarādyannirgamanaṃ tadretorūpāpekṣayā dvitīyaṃ janma dvitīyāvasthābhivyaktiḥ //3//
children.translated_text: And so, the emergence of this transmigrating being from the mother's womb, etc. in the form of a child is, relative to the semen-form [in the father], the second birth — the manifestation of the second state. [3]

children.text: START 2.4
children.translated_text: [Start of section 2.4]

children.text:
so 'syāyam ātmā puṇyebhyaḥ karmebhyaḥ pratidhīyate |
athāsyāyam itara ātmā kṛtakṛtyo vayogataḥ praiti |
sa itaḥ prayann eva punar jāyate |
tad asya tṛtīyaṃ janma || AitUp_2.4 ||
children.translated_text:
'This self of his is substituted for meritorious deeds.
Then this other self of his, having fulfilled his duties, having reached old age, departs.
He, departing from here, is born again.
That is his third birth.' [<s>AitUp</s> 2.4]

children.text: AitUpBh_2.4
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 2.4]

children.text:
asya pituḥ so 'yaṃ putrātmā puṇyebhyaḥ śāstroktebhyaḥ karmabhyaḥ karmaniṣpādanārthaṃ pratidhīyate pituḥ sthāne pitrā yatkartavyaṃ tatkaraṇāya pratinidhīyata ityarthaḥ /
tathā ca saṃprattividyāyāṃ vājasaneyake pitrānuśiṣṭaḥ -"ahaṃ brahmāhaṃ yajñaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 5 / 17) ityādi pratipadyata iti /
athānantaraṃ putre niveśyātmano bhāramasya putrasyetaro 'yaṃ yaḥ pitrātmā kṛtakṛtyaḥ kartavyādṛṇatrayādvimuktaḥ kṛtakartavya ityarthaḥ, vayogato gatavayā jīrṇaḥ sanpraiti mriyate /
sa ito 'smātprayanneva śarīraṃ parityajanneva tṛṇajalūkāvad dehāntaramupādadānaḥ karmacitaṃ punarjāyate /
tadasya mṛtvā pratipattavyaṃ yattattṛtīyaṃ janma /
children.translated_text:
This son-self of the father is substituted — for the purpose of accomplishing [those] meritorious deeds prescribed by scripture — in the father's place; that is, he is deputized by the father for the performance of what the father was to do. That is the meaning.
And thus, in the knowledge of the dying (<s>saṃprattividyā</s>) in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>, the son, instructed by the father, takes upon himself: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>, I am the sacrifice' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.5.17), etc.
Then, subsequently, having deposited his burden upon the son — this other self, which is the father's self, having fulfilled his duties, being freed from the three debts that were to be discharged, the meaning being 'having done what was to be done' — having reached old age, being aged and decrepit, departs, dies.
He, departing from here, leaving the body, taking up another body like a caterpillar [on a blade of grass], born [again] according to his accumulated <s>karma</s>, is born again.
That — the [state] to be obtained by dying — that is his third birth.

children.text:
nanu saṃsarataḥ pituḥ sakāśādretorūpeṇa prathamaṃ janma /
tasyeva kumārarūpeṇa māturdvitīyaṃ janmoktam /
tasyaiva tṛtīye janmani vaktavye pretasya pituryajjanma tattṛtīyamiti kathamucyate?
children.translated_text:
But the first birth of the transmigrating father was in the form of semen from [his own father].
The second birth was described as his own, in the form of a child from the mother.
When it should be stated that his own third birth [occurs upon death], how is it said that the birth of the deceased father is the third [birth]?

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ pitāputrayoraikātmyasya vivakṣitatvāt /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault, because the identity of the self of father and son is what is intended to be expressed.

children.text: so 'pi putraḥ svaputre bhāraṃ nidhāyetaḥ prayanneva punarjāyate yathā pitā /
children.translated_text: That son too, having deposited his burden on his own son, departing from here, is born again — just like the father.

children.text: tadanyatroktamitaratrāpyuktameva bhavatīti manyate śrutiḥ pitāputrayorekātmatvāt //4//
children.translated_text: What is said elsewhere is considered as said here too — thus the <s>śruti</s> holds, because of the identity of the self of father and son. [4]

children.text: START 2.5
children.translated_text: [Start of section 2.5]

children.text: evaṃ saṃsarannavasthābhivyaktitrayeṇa janmamaraṇaprabandhārūḍhaḥ sarvo lokaḥ saṃsāramasudre nipatitaḥ katañcidyadā śrutyuktamātmānaṃ vijānāti yasyāṃ kasyāñcidavasthāyāṃ tadaiva muktasarvasaṃsārabandhanaḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhavatīti -
children.translated_text: Thus, transmigrating through the manifestation of the three states, mounted upon the continuum of births and deaths, the entire world has fallen into the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). Whenever, in whichever state, one comes to know the Self as taught by the <s>śruti</s>, at that very moment one becomes freed from all the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s> and becomes one who has fulfilled all duties. Thus:

children.text:
tad uktam ṛṣiṇā -- garbhe nu sann anv eṣām avedamahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā |
śataṃ mā pura āyasīr arakṣannadha śyeno javasā nir adīyam |
iti |
garbha evaitac chayāno vāmadeva evam uvāca || AitUp_2.5 ||
children.translated_text:
'This was spoken by the sage: "While yet in the womb, I came to know all the births of these gods.
A hundred iron fortresses guarded me; then, like a hawk, with swiftness I flew forth."
Thus spoke <s>Vāmadeva</s>, even while lying in the womb.' [<s>AitUp</s> 2.5]

children.text: AitUpBh_2.5
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 2.5]

children.text: etadvastu tadṛṣiṇā mantreṇāpyuktamityāha -
children.translated_text: This very matter has also been stated by the sage through a mantra — thus he says:

children.text:
garbhe nu māturgarbhāśaya eva san /
nviti vitarke /
anekajanmāntarabhāvanāparipākavaśādeṣāṃ devānāṃ vāgagnyādīnāṃ janimāni janmāni viśvā viśvāni sarvāṇyanvavedamahamaho anubuddhavānasmītyarthaḥ śatamanekā bahvyo mā māṃ pura āyasīḥ āyasyo lohamayya ivābhedyāni śarīrāṇītyabhiprāyaḥ, arakṣannarakṣitavatyaḥ saṃsārapāśanirgamanādadhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
While yet in the womb — in the mother's womb itself, being [there].
'<s>Nu</s>' is used in the sense of deliberation.
Through the ripening of contemplation over many past lives, of these gods — <s>Vāk</s> (speech), <s>Agni</s>, and others — the births, all the births, all of them, I came to know — that is, 'I have become awakened' is the meaning. A hundred — many, numerous — iron [fortresses] — impenetrable like [walls] made of iron — the meaning is 'bodies'; guarded me, held me, from escaping the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, below [i.e., in bondage].

children.text: atha śyena iva jālaṃ bhittvā javasā ātmajñānakṛtasāmarthyena niradīyaṃ nirgato 'smi /
children.translated_text: Then, like a hawk [breaking through] a net, with swiftness — by the power acquired through Self-knowledge — I flew forth, I escaped.

children.text: aho garbha eva śayāno vāmadeva ṛṣirevamuvācaitat //5//
children.translated_text: Ah! Even while lying in the womb, the sage <s>Vāmadeva</s> thus spoke this. [5]

children.text: START 2.6
children.translated_text: [Start of section 2.6]

children.text: sa evaṃ vidvān asmāc charīrabhedād ūrdhvam utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvān kāmān āptvāmṛtaḥ samabhavat samabhavat || AitUp_2.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'He, thus knowing, rising upward from this dissolution of the body, having attained all desires in that heavenly world, became immortal — became immortal.' [<s>AitUp</s> 2.6]

children.text: AitUpBh_2.6
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 2.6]

children.text: sa vāmadeva ṛṣiryathoktamātmānamevaṃ vidvānasmāccharīrabhedāccharīrasyāvidyāparikalpitasya āyasavadanirvedyasya jananamanaṇādyanekānarthaśatāviṣṭaśarīraprabandhanasya paramātmajñānāmṛtopayogajanitavīryakṛtbhedāccharīrotpattibījāvidyādinimittopamardahetoḥ śarīravināśādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, the sage <s>Vāmadeva</s>, knowing the Self as described — from this dissolution of the body — of the body that is imagined through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), that is impenetrable like iron, whose continuum involves hundreds of calamities such as birth, death, and others — the dissolution [comes about] from the destruction of the body, meaning: from the cause that destroys the seeds of bodily arising such as <s>avidyā</s>, through the vigor born of the enjoyment of the nectar of the knowledge of the Supreme Self. That is the meaning.

children.text: ūrdhvaḥ paramātmabhūtaḥ sannadhobhāvātsaṃsārādutkramya jñānāvadyotitāmalasarvātmabhāvamāpannaḥ sannamuṣminyathokte 'jare 'mare 'mṛte 'bhaye sarvajñe 'pūrve 'napare 'nantare 'bāhye prajñānāmṛtaikarase pradīpavannirvāṇamatyagamatsvarge loke svasminnātmani sve svarūpe 'mṛtaḥ samabhavat /
children.translated_text: Rising upward — having become the Supreme Self, from the downward condition of <s>saṃsāra</s>, rising up — having attained the state of being the pure, immaculate Self of all, illuminated by knowledge — in that heavenly world, in the [world] as described: ageless, deathless, immortal, fearless, omniscient, without prior, without posterior, without interior, without exterior, of the single essence of the nectar of consciousness — like a lamp, he attained extinction (<s>nirvāṇa</s>) — in the heavenly world, in his own Self, in his own essential nature — he became immortal.

children.text: ātmajñānena pūrvamāptakāmatayā jīvanneva sarvānkāmānāptvetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: having already attained all desires through Self-knowledge — being one whose desires are already fulfilled while yet living. That is the meaning.

children.text: dvirvacanaṃ saphalasya sodāhaṇasyātmajñānasya parisamāptipradarśanārtham //6//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of 'became immortal'] is for the purpose of showing the completion of the Self-knowledge that is fruitful and illustrated [by the example of <s>Vāmadeva</s>]. [6]

children.text:
iti prathamādhyāye prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ
dvitīyaḥ adhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the first section of the first chapter.
The second chapter is complete.

children.text: START 3.1
children.translated_text: [Start of section 3.1]

children.text: bahmavidyāsādhanakṛtasarvātmabhāvaphalāvāptiṃ vāmadevādyācāryaparamparayā śrutyāvadyotyamānāṃ brahmavitpariṣadyatyantaprasiddhāmupalabhamānā mumukṣavo brāhmaṇa adhunātanā brahmajijñāsavo 'nityātsādhyasādhanalakṣaṇātsaṃsārādājīvabhāvād vyāvivṛtsavo vicārayanto 'nyonyaṃ pṛcchanti ko 'yamātmeti? katham -
children.translated_text: Perceiving the attainment of the fruit of being the Self of all — produced by the means of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> — as made known by the <s>śruti</s> through the teacher-lineage of <s>Vāmadeva</s> and other teachers, and as supremely well-established in the assemblies of the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — the seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣus</s>), the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the present time who desire to know <s>Brahman</s>, wishing to turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s> characterized by the impermanent means-and-end [relation] — which is [their condition] from birth — deliberating, ask one another: 'What is this Self?' How [do they ask]?

children.text:
ko 'yam |
ātmeti vayam upāsmahe |
kataraḥ sa ātmā |
yena vā paśyati yena vā śṛṇoti yena vā gandhāñ jighrati yena vā vācaṃ vyākaroti yena vā svādu cāsvādu ca vijānāti || AitUp_3.1 ||
children.translated_text:
'Who is this [Self]?
It is as the Self that we worship.
Which is the Self?
Is it that by which one sees, or that by which one hears, or that by which one smells odors, or that by which one articulates speech, or that by which one discerns the sweet and the not-sweet?' [<s>AitUp</s> 3.1]

children.text: AitUpBh_3.1
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 3.1]

children.text: yamātmānamayamātmeti sākṣādvayamupāsmahe kaḥ sa ātmeti yaṃ cātmānamayamātmeti sākṣādupāsīno vāmadevo 'mṛtaḥ samabhavattameva vayanamapyupāsmahe ko nu khalu sa ātmeti /
children.translated_text: This Self which we directly worship as 'this is the Self' — who is that Self? And that Self, directly worshipping whom as 'this is the Self,' <s>Vāmadeva</s> became immortal — we too worship that very [Self]. Who indeed is that Self?

children.text:
evaṃ jijñāsāpūrvamanyonyaṃ pṛcchatāmatikrāntaviśeṣaviṣayaśrutisaṃskārajanitā smṛtirajāyata /
'taṃ prapadābhyāṃ prāpadyata brahmemaṃ puruṣam' 'sa etameva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata' etameva puruṣam /
atra dve brahmaṇī itaretaraprātikūlyena pratipanne iti /
te cāsyapiṇḍasyātmabhūte /
tayoranyatara ātmopāsyo bhavitumarhati /
yo 'tropāsyaḥ kaḥ ātmeti viśeṣanirdhāraṇārthaṃ punaranyonyaṃ papracchurvicārayantaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Thus, preceded by the desire to know, as they questioned one another, a memory arose, generated by the impressions of the <s>śruti</s> relating to the specific subjects they had studied.
'With the soles of the feet he approached — <s>Brahman</s>, this person' — 'He split open this very suture and entered through this door' — this very person.
Herein, two [aspects of] <s>Brahman</s> have been understood as mutually opposed.
And these two are the very selves of this aggregate [body].
One of these two ought to be the Self worthy of worship.
Which is the Self to be worshipped here? — with the purpose of determining the specific [answer], they further questioned one another, deliberating.

children.text:
punasteṣāṃ vicārayatāṃ viśeṣavicāraṇāspadaviṣayā matirabhūt /
katham? dvevastuni asmin piṇḍa upalabhyete /
anekabhedabhinnena karaṇena yenopalabhate /
yaścaika upalabhyete /
karaṇāntaropalabdhaviṣayasmṛtipratisandhānāt /
tatra na tāvadyenopalabhate sa ātmā bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text:
Then, as they deliberated further, a thought arose regarding the subject matter for specific investigation.
How? Two things are perceived in this aggregate [body].
[First,] that by which one perceives — the instrument, divided into many forms.
[Second,] the one who perceives.
[The latter is known] through the synthesis and recognition of the objects perceived by different instruments.
Among these, that by which one perceives cannot be the Self.

children.text: kena punarupalabhata ityucyate yena vā cakṣurbhūtena rūpaṃ paśyati /
children.translated_text: But what is it by which one perceives? It is said: that by which, being the eye, one sees forms.

children.text: yena vā śruṇoti śrotrabhūtena śabdam, yena vā ghrāṇabhūtena gandhānājighrati, yena vā vākkaraṇabhūtena vācaṃ nāmātmikāṃ vyākaroti gauraśva ityevamādyāṃ sādhvasādhviti ca, yena vā jihvābhūtena svādu cāsvādu ca vijānātīti //1//
children.translated_text: That by which one hears — by which, being the ear, one [hears] sound; that by which, being the nose, one smells odors; that by which, being the organ of speech, one articulates speech consisting of names — such as 'cow,' 'horse,' and also 'good,' 'bad,' etc.; that by which, being the tongue, one discerns the sweet and the not-sweet. [1]

children.text: START 3.2
children.translated_text: [Start of section 3.2]

children.text: kiṃ punastadevaikamanekadhā bhinnaṃ karaṇam ityucyate -
children.translated_text: But what is this one instrument that appears as many? It is said:

children.text:
yad etad dhṛdayaṃ manaś caitat |
sañjñānam ājñānaṃ vijñānaṃ prajñānaṃ medhā dṛṣṭir dhṛtir matir manīṣā jūtiḥ smṛtiḥ saṅkalpaḥ kratur asuḥ kāmo vaśa iti sarvāṇy evaitāni prajñānasya nāmadheyāni bhavanti || AitUp_3.2 ||
children.translated_text:
'This heart and this mind —
<s>Saṃjñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>ājñāna</s> (comprehension), <s>vijñāna</s> (discernment), <s>prajñāna</s> (intelligence), <s>medhā</s> (wisdom), <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (vision), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>mati</s> (thought), <s>manīṣā</s> (reflection), <s>jūti</s> (impulse), <s>smṛti</s> (memory), <s>saṅkalpa</s> (resolve), <s>kratu</s> (will), <s>asu</s> (life-breath), <s>kāma</s> (desire), <s>vaśa</s> (mastery) —
all these are indeed names of <s>prajñāna</s> (pure consciousness).' [<s>AitUp</s> 3.2]

children.text: AitUpBh_3.2
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>AitUpBh</s> 3.2]

children.text:
yaduktaṃ purastātprajānāṃ reto hṛdayaṃ hṛdayasya reto mano manasā sṛṣṭā āpaśca varuṇaśca hṛdayānmano manasaścandramāḥ /
tadevaitaddhṛdayaṃ manaśca ekameva tadanekadhā /
etenāntaḥkaraṇenaikena cakṣurbhūtena rūpaṃ paśyati śrotrabhūtena śṛṇoti ghrāṇabhūtena jighrati vāgbhūtena vadati jihvābhūtena rasayati svenaiva vikalpanārūpeṇa manasā vikalpayati hṛdayarūpeṇādhyavasyati /
children.translated_text:
As was stated before: 'The seed of beings is the heart; the seed of the heart is the mind; created by the mind are the waters and <s>Varuṇa</s>; from the heart is the mind, and from the mind is the moon.'
That which is this heart and mind is one and the same, [appearing] in many forms.
By this one internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), being the eye, one sees forms; being the ear, one hears; being the nose, one smells; being speech, one speaks; being the tongue, one tastes; in its own form of ideation, as the mind, one ideates; in the form of the heart, one determines.

children.text: tasmātsarvakaraṇaviṣayavyāpārakamekamidaṃ karaṇaṃ sarvopalabdhyarthamupalabdhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is a single instrument that pervades the operations of all sense-objects — for the purpose of all perception, [serving] the perceiver.

children.text:
tathā ca kauṣītakīnāṃ"prajñayā vācaṃ samāruhya vācā sarvāṇi nāmānyāpnoti /
prajñā cakṣuḥ samāruhya cakṣuṣā sarvāṇi rūpāṇyāpnoti"(3 / 3) ityādi /
vājasaneyake ca -"manasā hyeva paśyati manasā śṛṇoti hṛdayena hi rūpāṇi jānāti"(bṛ.u.1 / 5 / 3) ityādi /
tasmād hṛdayamanovācyasya sarvopalabdhikaratvaṃ prasiddham /
tadātmakaśca prāṇo"yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā yo vai prajñā sa prāṇaḥ"(kauṣī.3 / 3) iti hi brāhmaṇam /
children.translated_text: And thus in the [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] of the <s>Kauṣītakins</s>: 'Mounting speech through consciousness (<s>prajñā</s>), one obtains all names through speech. Mounting the eye through consciousness, one obtains all forms through the eye' (<s>Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad</s> 3.3) and so forth. And in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>): 'For one sees with the mind, one hears with the mind; for one knows forms through the heart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.5.3) and so forth. Therefore, it is well-established that the heart-mind — denoted by [the word] 'heart' (<s>hṛdaya</s>) — is the instrument of all cognition. And <s>prāṇa</s> is identical with that [heart-mind], for there is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text: 'That which is <s>prāṇa</s> is <s>prajñā</s>; that which is <s>prajñā</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad</s> 3.3).

children.text:
karaṇasaṃhatirūpaśca prāṇa ityavocāma prāṇasaṃvādādau /
tasmādyatpadbhyāṃ prāpadyata tadbrahma tadupalabdhurupalabdhikaraṇatvena guṇabhūtatvānnaiva tadvastu brahmopāsyātmā bhavitumarhati /
pāriśeṣyādyasyopalabdhurupalabdhyarthaṃ etasya hṛdayasya manorūpasya karaṇasya vṛttayo vakṣyamāṇāḥ /
sa upalabdhopāsya ātmāno 'smākaṃ bhavitumarhatīti niścayaṃ kṛtavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: And we have stated at the beginning of the <s>prāṇa</s>-debate that <s>prāṇa</s> is of the nature of the aggregate of instruments. Therefore, that which was arrived at through the feet [of the proof] — that is <s>Brahman</s>. Since the instruments of cognition, being subsidiary to the cognizer, are not the reality [itself], they cannot be the Self to be worshipped as <s>Brahman</s>. By the process of elimination, that cognizer — for whose cognition the forthcoming modifications of this instrument called the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) in the form of the heart-mind are meant — he, the perceiver, is fit to be the Self to be worshipped by us: thus they arrived at the conclusion.

children.text:
tadantaḥkaraṇopādhisthasyopalabdhuḥ prajñārūpasya brahmaṇa upalabdhyarthā yā antaḥkaraṇavṛttayo bāhyāntarvartiviṣayaviṣayāstā imā ucyante /
saṃjñānaṃ saṃjñaptiścetanabhāvaḥ, ājñānamājñaptirīśvarabhāvaḥ vijñānaṃ kalādiparijñānam, prajñānaṃ prajñaptiḥ prajñatā, medhāgranthadhāraṇasāmarthyam dṛṣṭirindriyadvārā sarvaviṣayopalabdhiḥ, dhṛtirdhāraṇamavasannānāṃ śarīrendriyāṇāṃ yayottambhanaṃ bhavati - dhṛtyā śarīramudvahantīti hi vadanti, matirmananam, manīṣā tatra svātantryam. jūtiścetaso rujādiduḥkhitvabhāvaḥ smṛtiḥ smaraṇam, saṃkalpaḥ śuklakṛṣṇādibhāvena saṃkalpanaṃ rūpādīnām, kraturadhyavasāyaḥ asuḥ prāṇanādijīvanakriyānimittā vṛttiḥ, kāmo 'saṃnihitaviṣayākāṅkṣā tṛṣṇā, vaśaḥ strīvyatikarādyabhilāṣaḥ, ityevamādyā antaḥkaraṇavṛttayaḥ prajñaptimātrasyopalabdhurupalabdhyarthatvācchuddhaprajñānarūpasya brahmaṇa upādhibhūtāstadupādhijanitaguṇanāmadheyāni bhavanti saṃjñānādīni /
sarvāṇyeva etāni prajñānasya nāmadheyāni bhavanti na svataḥ sākṣāt /
tathā coktaṃ"prāṇanneva prāṇo nāma bhavati"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 7) ityādi //2//
children.translated_text:
Now are stated the modifications of the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), directed toward both external and internal objects, which serve as the means of cognition for that perceiver — of the nature of consciousness (<s>prajñā</s>), who is <s>Brahman</s> — stationed in the <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct) of the internal organ.
<s>Saṃjñāna</s> — awareness, the state of being conscious; <s>ājñāna</s> — command, the state of being a ruler; <s>vijñāna</s> — discernment, the knowledge of arts and the like; <s>prajñāna</s> — intelligence, the state of being wise; <s>medhā</s> — retentive power, the capacity to hold [the contents of] texts; <s>dṛṣṭi</s> — perception, the cognition of all objects through the sense-organs; <s>dhṛti</s> — fortitude, the sustaining by which the depleted body and senses are upheld — for they say 'one carries the body through fortitude'; <s>mati</s> — thinking, reflection; <s>manīṣā</s> — independence therein; <s>jūti</s> — the state of affliction of the mind such as pain and the like; <s>smṛti</s> — memory, recollection; <s>saṃkalpa</s> — volition, the conceiving of forms and the like in their white, dark, and other aspects; <s>kratu</s> — resolve, determination; <s>asu</s> — the activity that is the cause of vital functions such as breathing and the like; <s>kāma</s> — desire, longing for objects not present; <s>vaśa</s> — passion, the craving for intercourse with women and the like — these and other such modifications of the internal organ, being <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts) of <s>Brahman</s> which is of the nature of pure consciousness, serve as the means of cognition for the perceiver who is nothing but consciousness — and <s>saṃjñāna</s> and the rest become the designations of <s>Brahman</s> generated by those <s>upādhis</s>. All of these are names of <s>prajñāna</s> (consciousness) alone, not intrinsically or directly [names of anything else]. As it is stated: 'While breathing, it becomes known as <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.7) and so forth. ‖ 2 ‖

children.text: START 3.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Section 3.3]

children.text:
eṣa brahmā |
eṣa indraḥ |
eṣa prajāpatiḥ |
ete sarve devāḥ |
imāni ca pañca mahābhūtāni pṛthivī vāyur ākāśa āpo jyotīṃṣīty etānīmāni kṣudramiśrāṇīva bījānītarāṇi cetarāṇi cāṇḍajāni ca jārujāni ca svedajāni codbhijjāni cāśvā gāvaḥ puruṣā hastino yat kiñcedam prāṇi jaṅgamaṃ ca patatri ca yac ca sthāvaram |
sarvaṃ tat prajñānetram |
prajñāne pratiṣṭhitam |
prajñānetro lokaḥ |
prajñā pratiṣṭhā |
prajñānaṃ brahma || AitUp_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>Brahmā</s>. He is <s>Indra</s>. He is <s>Prajāpati</s>. These are all the gods. And these five great elements — earth, air, space, water, and luminaries — and these [creatures] that are, as it were, mixed with the minute: seeds of various kinds — egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and sprouting-born — horses, cattle, humans, elephants, and whatever else there is that breathes, that moves, and that flies, and whatever is stationary — all that is guided by consciousness (<s>prajñā</s>). It is established in consciousness. The world is guided by consciousness. Consciousness is the foundation. Consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>. ‖ <s>Aitareya Upaniṣad</s> 3.3 ‖

children.text: AitUpBh_3.3
children.translated_text: [<s>Aitareya Upaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 3.3]

children.text:
sa eṣa prajñānarūpa ātmā brahmāparaṃ sarvaśarīrasthaḥ prāṇaḥ prajñātmā /
antaḥkaraṇopādhiṣvanupraviṣṭo jalabhedagatasūryapratibimbavaddhiraṇyagarbhaḥ prāṇaḥ prajñātmā eṣa eva indro guṇāddevarājo vā eṣa prajāpatiryaḥ prathamajaḥ śarīrī /
yato mukhādinirbhedadvāreṇāgnyādayo lokapālā jātāḥ sa prajāpatireṣa eva /
ye 'pyete 'gnyādayaḥ sarve devā eṣa eva /
children.translated_text: This Self, of the nature of consciousness, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, abiding in all bodies — [he is] <s>Prāṇa</s>, the cognitive Self. Having entered the <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts) of the internal organs, like the reflection of the sun in different portions of water, he is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s>, the cognitive Self. He alone is <s>Indra</s>, by virtue of [his] quality [of lordship] — or the king of the gods. He is <s>Prajāpati</s>, the first-born embodied one. Since from him, through the apertures such as the mouth and the rest, the world-guardians like <s>Agni</s> and others were born — he is this very <s>Prajāpati</s>. And all those deities such as <s>Agni</s> and the rest — he is they all.

children.text: imāni ca sarvaśarīropādānabhūtāni pañca pṛthivyādīni mahābhūtānyannānnādatvalakṣaṇānyetāni kiñcemāni ca kṣudramiśrāṇi kṣudrairalpakairmiśrāṇi iva śabdo 'narthakaḥ sarpādīni bījāni kāraṇānītarāṇi cetarāṇi ca dvairāśyena nirdiśyamānāni /
children.translated_text: And these five great elements beginning with earth, which serve as the material of all bodies, characterized by the nature of food and eater — and these things that are mixed with the minute, that is, mixed with small, tiny [beings] — the word 'as it were' (<s>iva</s>) is meaningless [here, a mere particle] — [such as] serpents and the like; 'seeds' means causes; 'of various kinds' — they are indicated in two classes:

children.text:
kāni tāni! ucyante - aṇḍajāni pakṣyādīni, jārujāni jarāyujāni manuṣyādīni, svedajādīni yūkādīni, udbhijāni ca vṛkṣādīni, aśvā gāvaḥ puruṣā hastino 'nyacca yatkiñcedaṃ prāṇijātam, kiṃ tat? jaṅgamaṃ yaccalati padbhyāṃ gacchati /
yacca patatri ākāśena patanaśīlam /
children.translated_text: What are they? They are stated: egg-born — birds and the like; womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>) — humans and the like; moisture-born — lice and the like; sprouting-born — trees and the like; horses, cattle, humans, elephants, and whatever else there is that has life. What is that? That which moves — that which walks, going on feet; and that which flies — that which characteristically travels through the sky.

children.text:
yacca sthāvaramacalam /
sarvaṃ tadeṣa eva /
sarvaṃ tadaśeṣataḥ prajñānetram /
prajñaptiḥ prajñā tacca brahmaiva /
nīyate 'neneti netram prajñā netraṃ yasya tadidaṃ prajñānetram /
prajñāne brahmaṇyutpattisthitilayakāleṣu pratiṣṭhitaṃ prajñāśrayamityarthaḥ /
prajñānetro lokaḥ pūrvavat /
prajñācakṣurvā sarva eva lokaḥ prajñā pratiṣṭhā sarvasya jagataḥ /
tasmātprajñānaṃ brahma /
children.translated_text: And whatever is stationary, unmoving — all that is this [<s>Brahman</s>] alone. All that, without exception, is guided by consciousness (<s>prajñā</s>). <s>Prajñapti</s> (designation, consciousness) is <s>prajñā</s>, and that is <s>Brahman</s> itself. 'That by which one is guided (<s>nīyate</s>)' is <s>netra</s> (guide); consciousness (<s>prajñā</s>) is the guide — that which has consciousness as its guide is '<s>prajñānetra</s>' (guided by consciousness). 'Established in consciousness (<s>prajñāna</s>)' — that is, in <s>Brahman</s>, at the times of creation, sustenance, and dissolution — means having consciousness as its support. 'The world is guided by consciousness' — as explained before. Or: the entire world has consciousness as its eye. 'Consciousness is the foundation' — of the entire universe. Therefore, consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
tadetatpratyastamitasarvopādhiviśeṣaṃ sannirañjanaṃ nirmalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntamekamadvayaṃ"neti neti"iti (bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 26) sarvaviśeṣāpohasaṃvedyaṃ sarvaśabdapratyayāgocaram /
tadapyantaviśuddhaprajñopādhisaṃbandhena sarvajñamīśvaraṃ sarvasādhāraṇāvyākṛtajagadbījapravartakaṃ niyantṛtvādantaryāmisaṃjñaṃ bhavati /
tadeva vyākṛtajagatbījabhūtabuddhyātmābhimānalakṣaṇahiraṇyagarbhasaṃjñaṃ bhavati /
tadevāntaraṇḍodbhūtaprathamaśarīropādhimadvirāṭprajāpatisaṃjñaṃ bhavati /
tadbhūtāgnyādyupādhimaddevatāsaṃjñaṃ bhavati /
tathā viśeṣaśarīropādhiṣvapi brahmādistambaparyanteṣu tattannāmarūpalābho brahmaṇaḥ /
tadevaikaṃ sarvopādhibhedabhinnaṃ sarvaiḥ prāṇibhistārkikaiśca sarvaprakāreṇa jñāyate vikalpyate cānekadhā /
"etameke vadantyagniṃ manumanye prajāpatim /
indrameke 'pare prāṇamapare brahma śāśvatam"(manu.12 / 123) ityādyā smṛtiḥ //3//
START 3.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Section 3.4]

children.text: sa etena prajñenātmanāsmāl lokād utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvān kāmān āptvāmṛtaḥ samabhavat samabhavat || AitUp_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: With this cognitive Self (<s>prajñena ātmanā</s>), rising up from this world, and having attained all desires in that heavenly world, he became immortal — he became immortal. ‖ <s>Aitareya Upaniṣad</s> 3.4 ‖

children.text: AitUpBh_3.4
children.translated_text: [<s>Aitareya Upaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 3.4]

children.text: sa vāmadevo 'nyo vaivaṃ yathoktaṃ brahma veda prajñenātmanā yenaiva prajñenātmanā pūrve vidvāṃso 'mṛtā abhūvaṃstathāyamapi vidvānetenaiva prajñenātmanāsmāllokādutkramya ityādi vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: He — <s>Vāmadeva</s> or any other who knows <s>Brahman</s> as described — with that very cognitive Self (<s>prajñena ātmanā</s>), with which the wise ones of old became immortal — in the same way, this knower too, with this very cognitive Self, rising up from this world — and so forth; this has been explained.

children.text: asmāllokādutkramyāmuṣminsvarge loke sarvānkāmānāptvā amṛtaḥ samabhavatsamabhavadityomiti //4//
children.translated_text: Rising up from this world, having attained all desires in that heavenly world, he became immortal — he became immortal. <s>Oṃ</s>. ‖ 4 ‖

children.text: iti tṛtīye 'dhyāye prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the third chapter.

children.text: upaniṣad samāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Upaniṣad</s> is concluded.

children.text: oṃ tatsat
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ tat sat</s>.
